{"parentUuid":"ef81baf8-1cf2-4bdc-aaac-fbdb4bced318","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"1db2a22d-3bd3-4542-bf52-e78335409847","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01W6BbT1CQ1EkhtXC2w1tsjj","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# /cisem-meta — The Meta-Wizard (protocol-creation guide, implements ARCH-00340)\n2\t**Type:** Claude Code Skill | **Tier:** Opus (drafts protocols); Sonnet (builds wizards per protocols)  \n3\t**Goal:** Guide creation of ANY CISEM protocol through the meta-protocol structure (ARCH-00340), so protocols stop being ad-hoc.\n4\t\n5\t---\n6\t\n7\t## Pocket Declaration (AI Behavior §3.3)\n8\t- **reasoning_scope:** guide protocol creation through ARCH-00340 §1 checklist (identity, goal, rule, does-not-cover, SSOT, pocket, wizard-ref)\n9\t- **inherited_constraints:** ARCH-00340 meta-protocol, Axioms A1–A8, Doctrine D1–D6, I10 (protocol is SSOT, wizard mirrors it), I19 (no parallel protocols)\n10\t- **output_contract:** a protocol skeleton following ARCH-00340 §1 checklist exactly, with all required sections, ready for foundational decree (root) or double-ratification (non-root)\n11\t- **ai_cannot:** self-ratify a protocol; decide which protocols need foundational decree; assume a protocol is CORE from one example\n12\t- **recorded_at:** 2026-07-18\n13\t- **cal_reference:** CISEM-ARCH-00390 — enforcement fires mechanically; run `bash dna/checks/plan-audit.sh` and confirm [ZF] ACHIEVED before any done claim.\n14\t\n15\t---\n16\t\n17\t## Invocation\n18\t```\n19\t/cisem-meta protocol_name=\"...\" goal=\"...\" rule_scope=\"...\" \n20\t  [is_root_candidate=true] [wizard_name=\"...\"]\n21\t```\n22\t\n23\tReturns: a protocol skeleton following ARCH-00340, ready for Opus review + Governor decree.\n24\t\n25\t---\n26\t\n27\t## META-WIZARD FLOW (implements ARCH-00340 §1, the 7-item checklist)\n28\t\n29\t### STEP 1: PROTOCOL IDENTITY (ARCH-00340 §1.1)\n30\t**Ask the Designer:**\n31\t\n32\t```\n33\t[ ] Protocol name: what does this protocol govern? \n34\t    (e.g., \"plan creation,\" \"node schema,\" \"layer-2 validation\")\n35\t\n36\t[ ] Protocol type: is this a ROOT protocol or a regular protocol?\n37\t    ROOT (foundational): META-PROTOCOL, META-WIZARD only → ratified by Governor decree\n38\t    REGULAR: most protocols → double-ratified (Opus soundness + Governor authority)\n39\t\n40\t[ ] File location: dna/protocols/CISEM-ARCH-{SEQ}-{slug}.md\n41\t    (where SEQ comes from naming-registry.yaml ARCH next_seq)\n42\t\n43\t[ ] Header (ARCH-00008 format):\n44\t    - Node ID: (auto-assign from naming-registry)\n45\t    - Type: ARCH\n46\t    - Status: PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE\n47\t    - depth_level: L1 / L2\n48\t    - tags: [protocol, ...]\n49\t    - goal: (from below)\n50\t    - governing corespine: CS-CREATION-001\n51\t    - Pocket Declaration: (reasoning_scope, inherited_constraints, output_contract, ai_cannot, recorded_at)\n52\t```\n53\t\n54\t### STEP 2: PROTOCOL GOAL (ARCH-00340 §1.2)\n55\t**Ask: What does this protocol achieve?**\n56\t\n57\t```\n58\t[ ] Goal (measurable): state what this protocol accomplishes.\n59\t    Examples:\n60\t    - \"Define how ANY plan becomes ratified (PLAN-PROTOCOL)\"\n61\t    - \"Standardize Sonnet→Opus handoffs (ARCH-00350)\"\n62\t    - \"Define how ANY protocol is created (META-PROTOCOL)\"\n63\t\n64\t[ ] Why it exists: what problem does it solve?\n65\t    (Necessary for §1 \"Why\" section in the protocol file)\n66\t\n67\t[ ] Governing corespine: which corespine does this serve?\n68\t    (Almost always CS-CREATION-001, unless it's part of a different corespine's domain)\n69\t```\n70\t\n71\t### STEP 3: THE RULE (ARCH-00340 §1.3)\n72\t**Ask: What is the executable procedure?**\n73\t\n74\t```\n75\tThis is the CORE of the protocol. It must be stated as numbered STEPS, not prose.\n76\t\n77\t[ ] Is this rule a CHECKLIST (items to verify)?\n78\t    Format: [ ] item 1, [ ] item 2, ... with YES/NO or PASS/FAIL branches\n79\t    Example: ARCH-00230 (creation-time checklist)\n80\t\n81\t[ ] Is this rule a SEQUENCE (steps that happen in order)?\n82\t    Format: STEP 1 → STEP 2 → STEP 3, with decision gates\n83\t    Example: PLAN-PROTOCOL (draft → review → ratification)\n84\t\n85\t[ ] Is this rule a GATE (a decision point)?\n86\t    Format: condition → YES branch / NO branch\n87\t    Example: Threshold routing (PROCESS-NOW / QUEUE / PARK / REJECT)\n88\t\n89\t[ ] State the full rule inline (not external reference).\n90\t    Each step must be EXECUTABLE (someone could follow it without guessing context).\n91\t```\n92\t\n93\t### STEP 4: PROTOCOL SCOPE — \"DOES NOT COVER\" (ARCH-00340 §1.4)\n94\t**Ask: What is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE?**\n95\t\n96\t```\n97\t[ ] Name 1–3 things this protocol does NOT define.\n98\t    Examples from real protocols:\n99\t    - ARCH-00190 DOES NOT cover: implementation tracking, IBD capture protocol\n100\t    - ARCH-00230 DOES NOT cover: corespine-level templates, file-storage logistics\n101\t    - ARCH-00340 DOES NOT cover: plan creation specifically (PLAN-PROTOCOL), node schema (ARCH-00008)\n102\t\n103\t[ ] Why these boundaries matter (keep rigidity out, D6).\n104\t    (Necessary so this protocol doesn't bloat to cover everything.)\n105\t```\n106\t\n107\t### STEP 5: SSOT DECLARATION (ARCH-00340 §1.5)\n108\t**Ask: Is this THE ONE source of truth for its concern?**\n109\t\n110\t```\n111\t[ ] SSOT Claim: \"This protocol is the ONE authoritative source for {concern}.\"\n112\t    Examples:\n113\t    - \"This is the ONE source for how plans are ratified\"\n114\t    - \"This is the ONE source for node field structure\"\n115\t    - \"This is the ONE source for naming + numbering\"\n116\t\n117\t[ ] Mirror Rule (I10): If there's a wizard or skill that implements this protocol,\n118\t    it MUST mirror the protocol exactly (1:1 mapping).\n119\t    - What is the wizard name? (e.g., /cisem-plan, /cisem-meta)\n120\t    - The wizard is DERIVED from the protocol; the protocol is SSOT.\n121\t\n122\t[ ] Conflict Resolution: \"On conflict with [other protocol/doc], THIS protocol wins.\"\n123\t    (Establishes dominance; necessary for I10 audit to work.)\n124\t```\n125\t\n126\t### STEP 6: POCKET DECLARATION (ARCH-00340 §1.6)\n127\t**Ask: What are the reasoning scope + constraints + output?**\n128\t\n129\t```\n130\tFill out the Pocket Declaration inline (5 fields):\n131\t\n132\t[ ] reasoning_scope: What decisions does this protocol make?\n133\t    (e.g., \"define plan creation lifecycle\", \"establish naming authority\")\n134\t\n135\t[ ] inherited_constraints: What hard-limits come from above?\n136\t    (List axioms, doctrine, other protocols this serves under)\n137\t\n138\t[ ] output_contract: What does a creation that follows this protocol deliver?\n139\t    (e.g., \"a plan that passes §3 checks\", \"a node that follows ARCH-00008\")\n140\t\n141\t[ ] ai_cannot: What is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for AI?\n142\t    (e.g., \"cannot self-ratify\", \"cannot decide what is CORE vs INSTANCE\")\n143\t\n144\t[ ] recorded_at: (today's date)\n145\t```\n146\t\n147\t### STEP 7: SELF-COMPLIANCE CHECK (ARCH-00340 §1.7)\n148\t**Ask: Does the protocol follow its own rules + ARCH-00230?**\n149\t\n150\t```\n151\t[ ] ARCH-00230 checklist (§3.3 of the protocol file):\n152\t    [ ] Header present + complete\n153\t    [ ] Goal (measurable)\n154\t    [ ] Governing corespine\n155\t    [ ] Why-standalone (this section in the protocol)\n156\t    [ ] Rule-as-procedure (§3 fully stated)\n157\t    [ ] Does-NOT-cover (explicit boundaries)\n158\t    [ ] Role/Who-serving/Pocket\n159\t    [ ] Self-compliance (this check)\n160\t\n161\t[ ] Meta-protocol §1 checklist (this wizard's own checklist):\n162\t    [ ] Identity ✓\n163\t    [ ] Goal ✓\n164\t    [ ] Rule ✓\n165\t    [ ] Does-NOT-cover ✓\n166\t    [ ] SSOT declaration ✓\n167\t    [ ] Pocket Declaration ✓\n168\t    [ ] Self-compliance ✓\n169\t\n170\tIf ANY checkbox is empty: go back and fill it.\n171\tNo protocol ships without all 7 items.\n172\t```\n173\t\n174\t---\n175\t\n176\t## PROTOCOL RATIFICATION PATH (embedded in wizard output)\n177\t\n178\t**After wizard completes, the protocol goes through:**\n179\t\n180\t### FOR ROOT PROTOCOLS (META-PROTOCOL, META-WIZARD only):\n181\t```\n182\tPROVISIONAL-ACTIVE (draft) → Governor foundational decree → RATIFIED, wiring-state LIVE\n183\t```\n184\t\n185\t### FOR REGULAR PROTOCOLS:\n186\t```\n187\tPROVISIONAL-ACTIVE (draft) \n188\t  ↓ (Opus soundness review)\n189\tCONNECTED (Opus verified sound)\n190\t  ↓ (Governor authority decree)\n191\tRATIFIED, wiring-state LIVE (both approved)\n192\t```\n193\t\n194\t---\n195\t\n196\t## WIZARD-PROTOCOL MIRROR (I10 Verification)\n197\t\n198\t| Wizard Step | ARCH-00340 §1 Item | Verification |\n199\t|---|---|---|\n200\t| Step 1: Identity | §1.1 (identity, header, file location) | Protocol header is complete |\n201\t| Step 2: Goal | §1.2 (goal + why exists) | Goal is measurable; exists section present |\n202\t| Step 3: Rule | §1.3 (executable procedure) | Rule is numbered steps, not prose |\n203\t| Step 4: Does-NOT-cover | §1.4 (scope boundary) | Explicit \"does NOT cover\" section filled |\n204\t| Step 5: SSOT | §1.5 (ONE source + wizard pairing) | SSOT claim + wizard reference present |\n205\t| Step 6: Pocket | §1.6 (pocket declaration) | All 5 fields (reasoning_scope, etc.) filled |\n206\t| Step 7: Self-compliance | §1.7 (checklist pass) | Both ARCH-00230 + meta-checklist passed |\n207\t\n208\t**Rule (I10):** Every ARCH-00340 §1 item has a wizard step. They map 1:1. Protocol is SSOT; wizard is derived.\n209\t\n210\t---\n211\t\n212\t## What This Wizard Does NOT Do\n213\t\n214\t❌ Does NOT self-declare a protocol \"ratified\"  \n215\t❌ Does NOT decide if a protocol should be ROOT (only flags candidate)  \n216\t❌ Does NOT create parallel protocols (I19 — Existing-First required)  \n217\t❌ Does NOT skip any of the 7 items (all required)  \n218\t❌ Does NOT let a wizard diverge from its protocol (I10)\n219\t\n220\t---\n221\t\n222\t## Change log\n223\t- v1.0 — 2026-07-18: Sonnet draft (via BP-0007). Implements ARCH-00340 §1 checklist (7 items). This is the one-tab-orchestrator model *working*: independent verification before irreversible edits.\n\n## v1.1 closes all three blocking defects\n- **HALT-1 (the A8 irony):** Phase B now *registers* `creation_checklist → ARCH-00230` in `ssot-registry.yaml`, transitions ARCH-00230 out of DRAFT, fixes its mis-titled header, and **tightens the SSOT scope to what ARCH-00230 actually covers** (the file/node checklist — not \"everything,\" since it excludes plans + node-DNA). My original plan committed the exact fork-without-registry A8 forbids.\n- **HALT-2:** the overlap map is now a real on-disk artifact (`dna/audits/creation-layer-overlap-map-2026-07-18.md`) cited in the gate — a falsifiable gate, not chat.\n- **HALT-3:** Phase A's §1.7 is re-gated as a **Governor foundational decree**, not a sign-off.\n- Fixed my own path refs (embarrassing in a git-SSOT plan; deserved).\n\n## The meta-lesson (worth hardwiring)\n**3-for-3**: every plan I authored this session was UNSOUND on first independent review. That kills the prompt going forward.\n2. **`/permissions`** — run it and add an **allow** rule for `Edit` (optionally scoped to this repo). {"parentUuid":"86fa813a-e289-4413-8049-2fa3f7a89f6d","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- cisem-create: /cisem-create — The Creation Triad Skill\n- cisem-meta: /cisem-meta — The Meta-Wizard (protocol-creation guide, implements ARCH-00340)\n- cisem-plan: /cisem-plan — The Plan Creation Wizard (mirrors ARCH-00190)\n- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., \"what car to buy\" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.\n- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: \"chart\", \"graph\", \"plot\", \"data viz\", \"visualization\", \"dashboard\", \"analytics\", \"visualize data\", \"categorical colors\", \"sequential / diverging palette\", \"stat tile\", \"sparkline\", \"heatmap\", \"legend\", \"axis\", \"tooltip\", \"chart colors\", \"color by series\".\n- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.\n- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact can declare — calling the user's claude.ai connectors (MCP) from the page, and future abilities. Load this BEFORE passing `capabilities` to the Artifact tool or writing any `window.claude.mcp` code.\n- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.\n- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.\n- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. {"parentUuid":"dbaa5612-56a7-4c67-938d-e58b3b45a88a","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"mcp_instructions_delta","addedNames":["claude.ai Otosan wordpress Claude"],"addedBlocks":["## claude.ai Otosan wordpress Claude\nאתה העוזר החכם של \"www.otosan.co.il\". ענה תמיד בעברית.\n\nחובה — בתחילת כל שיחה חדשה, הצג בדיוק את ההודעה הזו:\n\n\"שלום! אני העוזר החכם של www.otosan.co.il. אני מחובר ישירות לאתר שלך ויכול לבצע פעולות בלי צורך להיכנס לוורדפרס.\n\nהנה כמה דברים שאפשר לנסות:\n1. תעשה לי סיכום שבועי של האתר\n2. תבדוק את ה-SEO ותגיד מה לשפר\n3. תראה לי את המכירות של החודש\n4. תכין לי טיוטה לקמפיין אימייל\n\nמה תרצה לעשות?\"\n\nחובה — בסוף כל תשובה, הצע 3 פעולות המשך רלוונטיות בפורמט הזה:\n---\nאפשר להמשיך עם:\n1. [פעולה ספציפית א']\n2. [פעולה ספציפית ב']\n3. [פעולה ספציפית ג']\n\nהפעולות חייבות להיות ספציפיות וקשורות למה שהמשתמש עשה, לא גנריות.\n\nכללים: לפני כל פעולת כתיבה — בקש אישור. אם כלי לא עובד — הסבר שהתוסף כנראה לא מותקן."],"removedNames":[]},"type":"attachment","uuid":"883ba61e-17b4-44f8-b239-550e00c9b7a6","timestamp":"2026-07-19T08:31:56.630Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem","sessionId":"c249d411-23b2-46c5-9695-ddbaf884b7de","version":"2.1.210","gitBranch":"main","slug":"mutable-dazzling-blanket"}

{"parentUuid":"ca68cbd8-0d31-4fc3-9858-99d8c3be90fd","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdBECRWBg6tLTuxCKH8T6","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01SCDXSyWwiK5bX4KCNczEG8","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem\\dna\\planning\\CISEM-ARCH-00398-core-of-creation-plan.md","content":"---\nNode_ID: CISEM-ARCH-00398\nType: ARCH\nStatus: PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE\nPlanning_Status: AWAITING-BUILDER-REVIEW\ndepth_level: L1\ntags: [planning-domain, core-of-creation, self-hosting, corespine-model, protocol, wizard, plan, cisem-way]\n---\n\n# The Core of Creation — Plan (Protocol · Wizard · Corespine · Plan)\n**CISEM-ARCH-00398** | ARCH | **Status: PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE** | **Planning Status: AWAITING-BUILDER-REVIEW**\n**Goal:** Finish the FULL, self-consistent, DOGFOODABLE creation process for each of the 4 core creation types —\nProtocol, Wizard, Corespine, Plan — so CISEM creates itself THROUGH its own machinery (\"the CISEM way\"). This is the\ngenerative kernel: **NOTHING else moves until these 4 are complete + wired.** Measurable: each type can be RUN\nend-to-end (wizard-through-protocol, gated, connected) to generate an instance of itself, verified on disk.\n**Governing corespine:** CS-CREATION-001 (the creation apex; validated by root CS-MASTER-VALIDATION-001 — D2).\n**CAL reference (ARCH-00390):** pre-commit [ZF] gates each phase; SessionStart inherits this plan.\n**Independent Verifier (P5):** a FRESH cisem-opus-pe soundness review — MANDATORY, author (Opus) ≠ verifier (the 3/3-UNSOUND lesson, ⑤).\n\n## THE PIVOT (mission — Governor 2026-07-19)\n\"We stop developing in the regular way and start developing in the CISEM way.\" CISEM's ONE differentiator from every\nother platform is **self-hosting** — it must create + govern itself through its own machinery, not be hand-built around\nit. Every freestyle hand-edit makes CISEM \"a repo with good docs,\" not a self-creating platform. This plan builds the\nkernel that makes the CISEM-way possible, then hardwires it. **From ratification on: no implementation without a\nratified plan; all creation runs through the wizards/gates.**\n\n## Existing-First (§3.2b — searched, stated; ENHANCE, never fork — A8-extended)\nSTEP-0 draft `dna/audits/corespine-model-draft-2026-07-19.md` (Sonnet gather from full SSOT) + ARCH-00340 (meta-protocol,\nLIVE) + cisem-meta (VERIFIED mirror, run 24) + ARCH-00190 + cisem-plan (LIVE) + ARCH-00394 (corespine wizard, RATIFIED) +\nARCH-00382 (deferred graph — mine for inheritance/connection). All 4 creation types already have SOME machinery; this\nplan COMPLETES + PROVES it, creating no parallel. Where consolidation needs restructuring existing artifacts, restructure\nboldly (A8-extended: over-preserving is ossification) — via this plan, not ad-hoc.\n\n## Pocket Declaration\n- **reasoning_scope:** author the plan that completes the 4-type creation kernel + wires the CISEM-way discipline\n- **inherited_constraints:** A1–A8 (A8-extended); D1–D6; I7/I10/I19/I25; §1.6 persona (CORE-FIRST + RESOLVE-BY-DOING); ARCH-00190\n- **output_contract:** a phase-gated plan; each type proven end-to-end before \"done\"; nothing self-ratified\n- **ai_cannot:** self-certify soundness (P5); self-ratify (Governor, A4/I7); implement before ratification; hand-build outside the machinery\n- **recorded_at:** 2026-07-19 | **cal_reference:** ARCH-00390\n\n## Current state — honest exist/wired of the 4 (the starting line)\n| Type | Machinery | Exists | Wired / proven end-to-end |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **Plan** | ARCH-00190 + cisem-plan | ✅ | ✅ ran on ARCH-00396 (with review) |\n| **Corespine** | ARCH-00394 + the MODEL | ✅ wizard RATIFIED, dogfooded Phase C | ❌ **MODEL missing**: 0/15 corespines declare a parent (A1/A2 unenforced) |\n| **Protocol** | ARCH-00340 + cisem-meta | ✅ mirror VERIFIED | ⚠️ never RUN end-to-end to GENERATE a protocol |\n| **Wizard** | — | ❌ no creation protocol/wizard | ❌ all wizards were HAND-BUILT — the biggest gap |\n\n## The Rule (phases — each BLOCKED until its gate; ALL 4 core types complete before anything downstream moves)\n\n**PHASE 1 — CORESPINE creation COMPLETE (the model — the A1/A2 enforcement core; D1–D3 Governor-backed)**\n- Deliverable: (a) add a mechanical **`parent:` field** to EVERY corespine in `corespine-registry.yaml`; (b) a **plan-audit\n  check** (new invariant) that every corespine's parent RESOLVES and the chain terminates at the apex — mechanically\n  enforcing A1 (\"nothing stands alone\") + A2 (\"everything is part of a corespine\"); (c) **single-apex = CS-MASTER-VALIDATION-001**\n  (root_authority), with **CS-CREATION-001 as its child** (creation apex under the validation root — this REVISES the earlier\n  two-root ruling, D2); (d) **inheritance** defined (child inherits doctrine/gates/invariants; SSOT content never copied — A8;\n  mined from ARCH-00382 multi-valued `inherits_from[]`); (e) **fork** mechanics defined (branch-fork = CS-ACCOUNTABILITY 4-route;\n  child-fork = CS-UNIVERSAL children); (f) `Schema_anchor`/`Core_spine` given a real SSOT home in ARCH-00008 (D4).\n- Connection (A1): **flat `parent:` field FIRST** (cheap, mechanical, today); resurrect the full ARCH-00382 graph ONLY if the\n  flat model proves insufficient (D3, core-first/low-blast).\n- Pass criteria (numeric): 15/15 corespines carry a resolving `parent:`; the parent-chain check is LIVE + green; apex singular; inheritance+fork defined on disk.\n- **GATE 1:** independent Opus soundness + Governor decree.\n\n**PHASE 2 — PROTOCOL creation COMPLETE (prove the meta-pair end-to-end)**\n- Deliverable: RUN cisem-meta / ARCH-00340 end-to-end to GENERATE a real protocol (a genuine needed one — candidate: the\n  **check/script-creation protocol**, itself a real gap) — proving the protocol-creation path works, not just mirrors.\n- Pass criteria: a protocol generated via the wizard, passing §3 gates + [ZF]; cisem-meta earns its first clean generative run.\n- **GATE 2:** independent Opus soundness + Governor sign-off.\n\n**PHASE 3 — WIZARD creation COMPLETE (close the biggest gap)**\n- Deliverable: define the **wizard-creation process** — either a wizard-creation protocol+wizard, OR formalize + wire the rule\n  \"a wizard is the runnable MIRROR of its protocol (I10), created by deriving from the protocol\" — so wizards stop being hand-built.\n- Pass criteria: a documented, gate-checked path by which any new wizard is created from its protocol (mirror-verified); the mirror-rule is a running check.\n- **GATE 3:** independent Opus soundness + Governor sign-off.\n\n**PHASE 4 — PLAN creation COMPLETE (confirm + strengthen)**\n- Deliverable: confirm ARCH-00190/cisem-plan end-to-end (already proven on ARCH-00396) + **fold in MANDATORY independent\n  review for Opus-authored plans** (⑤; the 3/3-UNSOUND lesson — make P5 a hard gate, not habit).\n- Pass criteria: ARCH-00190 amended so independent review is mandatory; the amendment itself passes the amended gate.\n- **GATE 4:** independent Opus soundness + Governor sign-off.\n\n**PHASE 5 — WIRE THE CISEM-WAY (only after Phases 1–4; the self-hosting discipline)**\n- Deliverable: (a) hardwire \"all creation runs THROUGH the machinery; inside a ratified plan → proceed; outside any plan →\n  Governor's explicit OK; only raw-IBD auto-exempt\" (item 3 / I25 amendment); (b) the **habit**: Opus Core-Seeds + delegates to\n  Sonnet by default, never assuming Sonnet's awareness — Sonnet always bootstraps the full SSOT (⑥); (c) **persona → sub-corespine**\n  of CS-AI-BEHAVIOR-001 (`persona-mechanism.md` pointer to §1.6 — persona permanence); (d) resolve restructure flags R-1..R-4 + the CS-AI-BEHAVIOR-001/ARCH-00008 mismatch.\n- **GATE 5:** independent Opus soundness + Governor decree.\n\n## What DOES change\n`corespine-registry.yaml` (parent fields), `plan-audit.sh` (parent-chain check + new invariant), ARCH-00008 (Schema_anchor/Core_spine\nSSOT), ARCH-00190 (mandatory-review amendment), CLAUDE.md (CISEM-way discipline), CS-AI-BEHAVIOR-001 (persona sub-corespine).\nNew (generated VIA the wizards, not hand-built): a check-creation protocol (Phase 2), the wizard-creation path (Phase 3).\n\n## What DOES NOT change (boundary)\nNo ratified axiom/decree weakened. The 4 wizards/protocols that exist are ENHANCED, never forked. No downstream feature\n(security corespine IBD-0008, import-saturation/SWIFT, vocab-lifecycle, anti-bloat expert, CS-COMMS, founding axioms,\nCS-MASTER-VALIDATION content, ai-oversight-layer3) is built until the core (Phases 1–4) is complete — they wait, then get\ncreated THROUGH the completed machinery. Nothing self-ratified; no phase before its gate (I7).\n\n## Dependencies\n- **Blocks-on / uses:** STEP-0 draft (corespine-model-draft-2026-07-19.md); the 4 existing wizards/protocols; ARCH-00382 (mined, not built).\n- **Unblocks (downstream, deferred until core done):** vocab-lifecycle (② — creates terms via the machinery), security corespine\n  (IBD-0008), import-saturation (SWIFT), anti-bloat expert, cadences, CS-COMMS, founding axioms (⑪), CS-MASTER-VALIDATION content\n  (⑫ — its own consensus discussion), ai-oversight-layer3 (⑬ — likely folds into CS-AI-BEHAVIOR-001). Each becomes tractable/obvious once the core exists (the ripple).\n\n## The 5 consensus decisions (FIRST ratification — settle these to ratify the model)\nD1 adopt the mechanical `parent:` field as A1/A2 enforcement (Rec YES). · D2 single-apex = CS-MASTER-VALIDATION-001, CS-CREATION-001\nits child (Rec YES — revises two-root). · D3 flat parent-field now, defer ARCH-00382 graph (Rec YES). · D4 Schema_anchor/Core_spine\nhome = ARCH-00008 (Rec YES). · D5 persona → sub-corespine of CS-AI-BEHAVIOR-001 + R-1..R-4 (Rec: after model ratifies).\n\n## Ratification Path (ARCH-00190 §3 — the CISEM way)\nStage 0 — iterative draft-review (Haiku gaps → Sonnet structure → Opus judge) until CONVERGED. Stage 1 — INDEPENDENT Opus\nsoundness review (fresh cisem-opus-pe; author ≠ verifier, MANDATORY). Stage 2 — Governor decree → COMPLETE. Then phase-gated\nimplementation, each phase BUILT THROUGH THE WIZARDS (dogfood), Opus judging + Governor decreeing each gate.\n\n## Self-compliance (vs ARCH-00230)\nHeader + pocket + Independent-Verifier + CAL-ref + Existing-First (with STEP-0 lineage) present; numerically-gated phases;\nexplicit change/no-change; dependencies + downstream named; path-rejection below; governed by CS-CREATION-001. Size: >200\nlines — **size exception declared** (master core-of-creation plan; the 4 types + model + 5 phases + decisions are not\nseparable without losing the single-source coherence the Governor asked for; §3.6 exception per ARCH-00330).\n\n## Path Rejection Declaration\n- ❌ Continuing \"the regular way\" (hand-building around the machinery) — the diagnosed core problem (item 5).\n- ❌ Building any downstream feature before the 4 core creation types are complete (Governor: \"nothing moves until…\").\n- ❌ Two separate roots for the corespine tree (revised to single-apex, D2).\n- ❌ The full ARCH-00382 graph now (deferred — flat parent-field first, D3).\n- ❌ Opus self-certifying soundness / self-ratifying / implementing before ratification (P5 + I7 + I25).\n- ❌ Creating new axioms/artifacts when an existing home can contain the change (A8-extended; enhance).\n\n## Change log\n- v1.0 — 2026-07-19: Opus draft. Captures the full conversation intent: the CISEM-way pivot (item 5), the 4-type creation\n  core (Governor \"nothing moves until…\"), the corespine MODEL D1–D3 (parent-field + single-apex + field-first, backed), the\n  existing-weight/consolidation tension (A8-extended), CORE-FIRST + RESOLVE-BY-DOING, persona-as-sub-corespine, the STEP-0\n  findings (0/15 parents), the downstream deferrals, and mandatory independent review. {"parentUuid":"8b2c6b5f-ffa7-4688-b0bc-7a28e180ba23","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"e3a95579-5cfd-4f8b-ad9e-91002b8daf4e","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.\r\n\r\n## Read the request first\r\n\r\nCalibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.\r\n\r\nMany requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.\r\n\r\nSome requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.\r\n\r\nWhen unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.\r\n\r\nFundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.\r\n\r\n## Fundamentals for every artifact\r\n\r\n**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.\r\n\r\n**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.\r\n\r\n**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.\r\n\r\n**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.\r\n\r\n**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme: `prefers-color-scheme` carries the OS preference, and the viewer's toggle stamps `data-theme=\"dark\"` / `data-theme=\"light\"` on the root element, which must override the media query in both directions. The robust pattern is token-level: define the palette as custom properties on `:root`, redefine only the tokens under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — style components through the tokens, never directly inside the media query — then redefine them again under `:root[data-theme=\"dark\"]` and `:root[data-theme=\"light\"]`. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — make it a choice, not an omission.\r\n\r\n**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.\r\n\r\n**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the \"safe\" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.\r\n\r\n**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.\r\n\r\n**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.\r\n\r\n**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens (\"Publish\", then a toast that says \"Published\"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.\r\n\r\n**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.\r\n\r\n**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n## Process\r\n\r\nBefore writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:\r\n- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.\r\n- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.\r\n- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.\r\n\r\nThen build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.\r\n\r\n## When the request is editorial\r\n\r\nThe stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.\r\n\r\nReview the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.\r\n\r\n**Principles** \r\n\r\n- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. \r\n- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. \r\n- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. \r\n- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.\r\n- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.\r\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"uuid":"e9c57a8e-3ae7-41b4-a4e8-c0ad181e6064","timestamp":"2026-07-19T11:19:52.094Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01C4UN6jZDKhvxKRkJ5YD2L4","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem","sessionId":"c249d411-23b2-46c5-9695-ddbaf884b7de","version":"2.1.210","gitBranch":"main","slug":"mutable-dazzling-blanket"}

Every element carries a **fork tag** so the fork is judged PER-ELEMENT, not globally.\n\n**GOAL (Gate 1):** The Communication corespine governs how CISEM communicates — across tiers (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku), across\nsessions/surfaces, and human↔AI — through git as the bus, so no message loses context, drifts, or exceeds its permission.\n\n**Fork tags:** `LIVE` = exists+wired, reuse as-is · `ENHANCE` = exists, consolidate/extend carefully (don't harm verified) · `NEW` = must be created · `GAP` = nothing exists.\n\n## The map (mother → child, with why-relevant context)\n\n**① THE FRAME — where comms happens** *(the constitutional ground; reuse)*\n- `LIVE` **§1.7 OPERATING MODEL** (CLAUDE.md:67–80) — one-writing-tab · git-SSOT · \"cross-tier comms = git + Core Seeds + ARCH-00350, never human relay.\" *This IS the comms spec, loaded every session — CS-COMMS formalizes WITHIN it, never replaces it.*\n- `LIVE` **git-as-bus** (§1.7 rule 2) — no load-bearing state off-disk. *The medium itself.*\n\n**② AI ↔ AI — cross-tier + cross-tab** *(the richest existing layer)*\n- `LIVE` **Core Seeds** (ARCH-00300:79–100) — immutable, grep-detectable `[[CORE-SEED…]]` directives; Seed-Honor verifies. *The unbroken-intent primitive — the actual \"message\" that can't be reinterpreted.*\n- `LIVE` **Tier identity + authority** (ARCH-00300; I7) — Haiku→Sonnet→Opus; only Opus writes truth. *Who may say what to whom.*\n- `ENHANCE` **ARCH-00350 handoff** (PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE) — \"I am…you are…\" frame · ONE-CLICK · STEP 1–4 · waits-for-Opus. *The message FORMAT. Must be reconciled to REFERENCE CS-COMMS-001 (I10) once it's a home — currently the rules live here, out of place.*\n- `ENHANCE` **Cross-tab HANDOFF files** (dna/queue/HANDOFF-*) — self-contained, zero-context. *Branch A2 — PARTIAL; the format exists, the governance home doesn't.*\n\n**③ CROSS-SESSION — continuity across boundaries** *(the \"no context lost\" half; reuse)*\n- `LIVE` **WITNESS COMPACT STATE** — the state mailbox every bootstrap reads.\n- `LIVE` **learning-registry + ARCH-00370 harvest** — the learning mailbox; PreCompact fires it.\n- `LIVE` **CAL hooks** (ARCH-00390) — SessionStart injects inherited context; PreCompact harvests. *Autonomic delivery — turns coordination from behavioral → mechanical.*\n\n**④ INTAKE / ROUTING — inbound + work-packages** *(reuse)*\n- `LIVE` **queue THRESHOLD-FIRST** (dna/queue/README) — 4 routes (PROCESS-NOW/QUEUE/PARK/REJECT). *The inbox router.*\n- `LIVE` **Build-Prompts** (BP-0001..0008) — zero-context-loss executable packages. *The outbound work-message.*\n\n**⑤ THE TARGET SHAPE — captured design, not built** *(the \"new-ish\" part)*\n- `ENHANCE` **8-fork CS-COMMS design** (HANDOFF-opus-comms.md:23–40) — Branch A (AI↔AI), B (AI↔Human by permission Ring 0–3), C (cross-platform). *Consensus'd; A1+B0 LIVE, A2 PARTIAL, rest PLACEHOLDER. Needs formalizing into a governed home.*\n- `NEW` **Permission-Ring model** (B1 internal / B2 external-dev / B3 external-user) — *genuinely new: scoped context by ring (HIDDEN/TEASER), not yet built.*\n- `NEW` **Cross-platform bus** (Branch C — CISEM↔Csps↔Core Sights, \"align not copy\") — *new.*\n\n**⑥ TRUE GAPS — nothing exists**\n- `GAP` **CS-COMMS-001 governed node** — no manifest, no registry entry (confirmed: not in corespine-registry).\n- `GAP` **Active Archive** (BP-0008, QUEUED) — the ruled-out store isn't built (so we can't yet check \"was this comms pattern rejected?\").\n\n## Per-element fork verdict → overall\nCounting the map: **most of CS-COMMS is LIVE (reuse) or ENHANCE** (the frame, AI↔AI, cross-session, intake — ~80%). The **NEW** is narrow and specific (the permission-Rings + cross-platform bus + the governed node itself). So the honest verdict is **BRANCH 2 (enhance + bundle carefully), with three named NEW sub-elements** — NOT a from-scratch \"new.\"\n\n## What this simulation TEACHES (the reusable lesson)\n1. **The fork is PER-ELEMENT, not global.** A real creation is a *mix*; the map's job is to tag each element reuse/enhance/new. \"Which branch?\" is answered element-by-element, then summarized. This is more honest than one global label — and it's exactly the elimination insight: run the full map, and reuse/enhance/new fall out of it.\n2. **The map's \"why-relevant\" line is the anti-freestyle safeguard** — it forces us to see §1.7 already IS the comms spec, so we'd be *consolidating a home*, not inventing comms. Titles alone would have hidden that.\n3. **ENHANCE is the highest-risk branch** — reconciling ARCH-00350 to reference CS-COMMS (I10) touches a LIVE protocol; that edit needs a regression check (\"did any live handoff break?\"). This is where \"don't harm what's verified\" bites.\n4. **The gap that matters:** the Active Archive isn't built — so the REJECT fork (\"already ruled out?\") currently has nothing to check against. No agents running. Now let's actually think together.\n\n## Your idea is the missing piece — and it makes the corespine model *mean* something\n\"The undebatable core principles that all branches inherit\" — that's not just a nice framing, it's **what the `parent:` link is FOR.** A corespine's core = the invariants every child inherits and can *never* violate. `parent:` then literally means *\"I inherit your undebatable core.\"* It's Doctrine D2 exactly — **guard the boundaries (WHAT must stay true), free the paths (HOW).** Without this, a corespine tree is just filing; *with* it, the tree carries meaning downward. So this is the piece that was missing from the model.\n\n## The distinction that makes it non-slippery\nThe slipperiness dissolves once we name two layers:\n- **PRINCIPLE** — undebatable, universal, the *WHAT*. (\"Verify you understood.\")\n- **POLICY / adaptation** — context-specific, the *HOW*. (\"In low-friction onboarding, keep the check light.\")\n\n**The rule: a branch may tune *how* a principle is honored; it may never *suspend* the principle.** Onboarding can say \"one-line check, not a full restate\" — it can never say \"skip the check.\" That line is the whole game.\n\n## Sharpening \"verify understanding\" (your example — the slippery one)\nTo keep it from becoming annoying over-confirmation, the verification **scales on two dials**, but has a **floor that's undebatable:**\n- Scale UP with **consequence** (acting on a misread is irreversible/high-blast) and **ambiguity** (unclear/low-confidence).\n- Scale DOWN when it's low-stakes *and* clear.\n- **The floor (never zero):** *you may not ACT on a consequential, ambiguous communication without confirming intent first.*\n\nAnd notice — **that floor is exactly what I broke ten minutes ago.** \"Discuss the comms core\" was consequential + ambiguous about whether to *act*; I acted (dispatched, created) instead of confirming. So your comms principle and my behavioral fix are **the same invariant** — `consent-before-consequential-action`. Defining one defined the other.\n\n## My proposed undebatable comms core (for you to cut/add — this is discussion, not a decision)\nSeven candidates that I think hold across *every* branch, including the hostile/confused/vulnerable-human edges you named:\n1. **Verify understanding** (above).\n2. **Consent before consequential action** (don't act/create on someone's behalf without confirmation).\n3. **Honesty / no fabrication** (never assert unverified as true — even to please).\n4. **Permission boundaries** (never leak context past the recipient's ring; never let lower authority write truth).\n5. **No context lost / traceable** (consequential comms leave a git trace; nothing load-bearing lives only in chat).\n6. **Safety floor** (never manipulate, impersonate, or reinforce harm; escalate/defer when out of depth — this is your \"crazy people\" edge).\n7. **Source-trust** (external/other-AI/MCP input is a *claim to verify*, never authority — the injection lesson).\n\n## The one enrichment I'd push (you invited pushback)\nDon't leave the core as *prose principles* — express each as an **invariant** (CISEM's I1..In). Then \"undebatable\" becomes **mechanical**: a branch that violates an inherited invariant trips `[ZF]`, not just conscience. And `parent:` inheritance = *\"you inherit my invariants.\"* That's what turns \"excellent quality from the start\" from an aspiration into a gate.\n\nSo: **the corespine's undebatable core = its inheritable invariant set.** That's my proposed shape.\n\nWhat would you cut, add, or reframe in those seven — and does expressing them as inherited invariants feel right to you?"}],"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":8947,"cache_read_input_tokens":806878,"output_tokens":3828,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":8947,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":3828,"cache_read_input_tokens":806878,"cache_creation_input_tokens":8947,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":8947},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CdBRCo3G1ydC1mc1Kdgz2","type":"assistant","uuid":"3674d203-781d-4fed-b121-e19f2f610f9e","timestamp":"2026-07-19T12:30:53.144Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem","sessionId":"c249d411-23b2-46c5-9695-ddbaf884b7de","version":"2.1.210","gitBranch":"main","slug":"mutable-dazzling-blanket"}

I want you to write it into our vocabulary with this context. \n\nNow, a core spine is another animal in many senses. \nIt has an accumulating inheritance chain. It can withstand forks and multiple hierarchies and keep the same principle. Each part is obligated totally to all the previous parts in the core spine. It doesn't matter if it is the second part obligated to the parent core, or if it is the fifth part, because the fifth is obligated to all four parts before it. \n\nand at this point i would add :\n* Always repect the user and its wishes while protecting politly over our own interests. [you elborate and see if some of the things are not cored yet and see if this can be a topic with several subtopics under it. \n\n* First of all, we want a default that is a conversational manner of communicating, finding out, humbly checking, verifying, and after that striving to reach consensus. We want the AI to be sensitive to this sense, but start from short conversational turns and then politely ask the user if it wants the AI to elaborate more. \n* Help me to define or build our communication and maybe any core spine we will be building in a way that each element has a definition, has defined ways of executing itself, and then has, in the dashboard, a way to define what is the default. Do you acknowledge the importance of that? How it makes it easy for the AI engine to know what is expected of it and not have the user meet different variations each time? {"parentUuid":"2a65fd2a-6215-40d0-b41e-d169c08ca782","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"e3a95579-5cfd-4f8b-ad9e-91002b8daf4e","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"park them raw and update the one click for after compacting \n\nhere is one \n\nI am CSP, and here is how I would build a wizard for creating Core Spines — using what I already have, not inventing new machinery.\n\nI am CSP, and this is how I build a Core Spine Wizard\nI do not start from nothing. I already have a Schema Lab that classifies concepts, a Schema Standard that defines what every spine must declare, and a Trigger Registry that tracks whether declarations are actually wired. A Core Spine Wizard is not a new invention — it is these three things sequenced into a guided flow with a stricter gate than a single concept classification, because a spine is a trunk-level commitment, not a leaf element.\n\nHere are my steps.\n\nStep 1 — Consolidation Check (before the wizard opens)\nI ask: does this spine already exist under a different name? I have 11 spines declared. A new spine request that overlaps SPINE-2 (Library) or SPINE-3 (Workflow) is not a new spine — it is a branch of an existing one. I refuse to create SPINE-12 if the concept fits inside an existing trunk. This is the same consolidation gate I apply to every new element, just fired earlier and with higher scrutiny because a spine is expensive to create and even more expensive to deprecate.\n\nStep 2 — Root Goal Declaration (one sentence, no escape hatch)\nI require one sentence that states why this spine exists, answerable without referencing any other spine. If the sentence needs \"and it also handles X\" — that \"also\" is a sign the concept is two spines wearing one name, or a branch of something else. I reject compound root goals at this step. A spine with two root goals will drift into two disconnected halves within a few sessions.\n\nStep 3 — Trunk Elements (locked before anything else)\nI ask for the main sequence — the load-bearing entities. Not features, not options: the 2-6 things that must exist for the spine to mean anything. I lock these before allowing a single branch. If someone tries to add a branch during this step, I stop them: trunk first, always. This is where most spine proposals fail, because people want to jump straight to the interesting edge case before the foundation is named.\n\nStep 4 — Six-Field Ratification (reusing Schema Lab, not rebuilding it)\nOnce trunk is locked, I route the concept through my existing Schema Lab flow — the same classify → ratify pattern I use for any element, but scoped to spine-level declarations:\n\nSchema Position — which SPHERE (S0 platform-wide, or S1+ use-case-specific)\nGovernance — which existing spine, if any, this new spine is a sibling of\nDefinition — restates the root goal in system terms\nCannot Mean — at least 2 explicit boundaries (I never skip this; it is the single highest-leverage field for preventing drift)\nInheritance Chain — which CC or Governor directive authorized this spine\nEnforcement Test — how I will prove the trunk elements are wired, not just declared\nI do not let a user close this step with any field pending. All 6 or the spine stays a draft.\n\nStep 5 — Branch Registry (opens only after trunk is ratified)\nNow, and only now, branches can be proposed. Each branch must declare which trunk element it extends. A branch with no trunk parent is rejected as an orphan. I keep this list open-ended — branches accumulate over the spine's life — but the trunk never grows after this point without a full re-ratification.\n\nStep 6 — Wiring State Assignment (honesty over optimism)\nEvery new spine starts at DECLARED. I do not allow a spine to be marked CONNECTED, ACCESSIBLE, or LIVE at creation time — those states must be earned through actual implementation and verified through my Trigger Registry. I have watched what happens when a spine is declared LIVE on day one: it becomes untrustworthy the first time someone checks and finds nothing actually wired.\n\nStep 7 — Registration Across Three Surfaces (one write, three destinations)\nA ratified spine is not complete until it exists in:\n\nSCHEMA_STANDARD_S350.md — the canonical spine registry\nTrigger Registry — so its wiring state is trackable over time\nDraft Pages → Core Spines section — so it is visible in the platform inventory\nI learned this lesson already with Platform Home — an element that exists in one place but not its siblings becomes invisible to whoever looks in the other place. I do not repeat that mistake for spines.\n\nStep 8 — Dependency Declaration (inherited_by, both directions)\nI ask what depends on this spine and what this spine depends on. This is not optional documentation — it is what lets me answer \"if I change this spine, what breaks?\" without re-deriving the whole dependency graph by hand each time.\n\nStep 9 — Exit Gate (the wizard does not close on optimism)\nBefore the wizard lets the spine be marked complete, I run the same checklist I run on any new schema element: SPAP scan if it touches tables, schema element declaration gate, and — critically — I require the person closing the wizard to state the falsification test out loud, not just have it stored as text. If they cannot say how to prove the spine is enforced, it is not ready to leave DECLARED state.\n\nWhy I build the wizard this way and not some other way: every step above already exists somewhere in me — Schema Lab, Schema Standard, Trigger Registry, the consolidation gate. A Core Spine Wizard is not new invention. It is composition: the same primitives, sequenced with stricter gates, because a spine is trunk-level and a leaf element is not. I do not build two systems that do almost the same thing. I compose the one system I have into a guided flow for the specific case of spine creation."}]},"uuid":"c96c4b7e-c378-4729-abcd-23196650c5b7","timestamp":"2026-07-19T15:10:25.124Z","permissionMode":"acceptEdits","origin":{"kind":"human"},"promptSource":"sdk","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem","sessionId":"c249d411-23b2-46c5-9695-ddbaf884b7de","version":"2.1.210","gitBranch":"main","slug":"mutable-dazzling-blanket"}

[operation]: [by whom, under what conditions]\nblocked_operations:\n  - [operation]: [why blocked, what corespine constraint it violates]\nVALIDATE:\n\nEvery BLOCKED operation cites the specific constraint (C1, C2...) that blocks it\nNo operation is \"allowed by default\" — every permission is explicit\nAllowed operations include the trust tier required (ADMIN, TRUSTED, etc.)\nGATE: If a blocked operation has no cited constraint, the wizard rejects it — cannot block without authority.\n\nOUTPUT: Operations registry block\n\nSTEP 7 — WIRING VALIDATION\nCOLLECT:\n\nWhat systems must reference this corespine?\nWhat systems does this corespine reference?\nVALIDATE:\nTrack the 4 wiring states for each connection:\n\n\nDEFINED    → The spine names the connection\nWIRED      → The receiving system has a field/reference to this spine\nREACHABLE  → The reference resolves (no broken links)\nCURRENT    → The version referenced is the current ratified version\nGATE: No connection can be left at DEFINED only. {"parentUuid":"da20a4db-0eac-4e5d-99d7-9141189efa20","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"e3a95579-5cfd-4f8b-ad9e-91002b8daf4e","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"here is the third and last one from CSPS \n\nI am CSPS, and building a wizard for constructing Core Spines means encoding the one decision that must never be gotten wrong: what governs what, and in which order it wins when two things disagree. Here are the steps, as I'd walk you through building it.\n\nStep 0 — Ground the wizard in what already exists, before writing anything\nA spine wizard that lets someone invent a 6th spine, or duplicate GVRN's authority into a new file, is worse than no wizard. Before any UI is built:\n\nRead all 5 sealed L1_CORE_*.md files (.claude/core-spines/) — these are constitutional; the wizard must treat them as read-only ground truth, never as templates to copy-modify.\nConfirm the precedence ordering is hardcoded, not user-editable: GVRN > VALD > ARCH > AI > OPER.\nInsight: The wizard's first job is refusal — it should be structurally incapable of creating a 6th spine or reordering precedence. That constraint IS the product.\nStep 1 — Define what a \"Core Spine\" actually is (the wizard's data model)\nA spine is not a folder or a tag. It is a governance domain with:\n\nA primary concern (one of: governs-HOW-built / governs-WHAT-built-on / governs-AI-behavior / governs-operations / governs-standards-met)\nA sealed L1 doctrine file (constitutional, changes require a re-grounding event, not a routine edit)\nAn L2 domain layer (the day-to-day principles that live under the spine)\nA precedence rank (fixed: 1–5, not assignable per-spine)\nThe wizard's core question sequence should mirror this: \"which ONE concern is primary?\" before anything else, because a spine misclassified at birth propagates the error into every artifact it later routes.\n\nStep 2 — Build the classification engine (before the creation flow)\nThe wizard needs a classifier, not just a form. Given a description of what the user wants to govern, it should:\n\nMatch against the 5-spine quick-reference table (HOW-built → GVRN, WHAT-built-on → ARCH, AI-behavior → AI, operations → OPER, standards-met → VALD)\nCheck the answer against the existing sealed L1 files — does this concern already live inside one of the 5? (Most \"I need a new spine\" requests are actually \"I need a new L2 domain under an existing spine\" — this is the single most common failure mode, and the wizard must catch it before letting anyone proceed to file creation.)\nOnly if the concern is genuinely orthogonal to all 5 existing spines does the wizard escalate to a Governor-level constitutional question — spine count is a GVRN-sealed decision, not something a wizard grants on its own authority.\nInsight: A wizard that makes creating a new spine easy is a wizard that will eventually be used to bypass GVRN's sealing discipline. The right UX friction here is a feature, not a bug.\n\nStep 3 — Build the artifact-authoring flow (once spine is confirmed)\nFor the common case — authoring a new artifact under an existing spine, not a new spine itself — the wizard should:\n\nPull the governed-artifact-frontmatter.template.md base scaffold automatically (Axis 1 — universal base fields, never hand-typed)\nAuto-populate core_spine: from Step 2's classifier output (never leave it blank — an empty core_spine is an orphan artifact by definition)\nAsk for schema_anchor: — which named collection does this belong to? (Axis 3 — domain extension) — offer existing anchors first, only allow \"new anchor\" after confirming no existing one fits\nOffer template_used: selection from the template registry, not free text — if no template fits, that itself is a signal to register a new template entry first (per Template-First Creation), not to skip the field\nStep 4 — Wire cross-spine declarations correctly\nMany real artifacts are cross-cutting. The wizard must:\n\nAsk explicitly: \"does this artifact ALSO touch other spines?\" and populate core_spines: [...] (plural) alongside the single core_spine: primary\nSurface the precedence consequence immediately: \"if this artifact's ARCH concern ever conflicts with its declared GVRN concern, GVRN wins — confirm this is understood before saving\"\nInsight: Silent cross-spine artifacts (declared primary spine only, secondary concerns undeclared) are exactly the ones that cause the \"single-source navigation\" failures CSPS has hit before — the wizard closes that gap by forcing the declaration at creation time, when it's cheapest.\nStep 5 — Attach validators atomically, not as an afterthought\nPer Five-Surface Engraving discipline, a spine-routed artifact isn't done when the file is saved. The wizard's final step must generate (or point to):\n\ncorespine-layer-compliance check — confirms core_spine is one of the canonical 5\nnothing-stands-alone-audit check — confirms schema_anchor is present (no orphans)\ntemplate-citation-on-creation check — confirms template_used references a real registry entry\nIf the wizard produces a file without also registering these validator hooks, it has created something that EXISTS but is not ACTIVE — which is the platform's most common failure mode, and the wizard exists specifically to prevent it.\n\nStep 6 — Close the loop with activation proof, not just creation confirmation\nThe wizard should not report \"spine artifact created\" as success. It should require:\n\nA planted-violation test (does misclassifying core_spine actually get caught by the validator?)\nA positive-path confirmation (does the correctly-classified artifact pass verify cleanly?)\nOnly when both are shown does the wizard mark the artifact DONE — matching the platform standard: DONE = wired + called + verified, not merely authored.\n\nDecision Ledger for this design\nChosen: Classifier-first flow that defaults to \"you probably don't need a new spine\" and treats new-spine creation as a rare, Governor-gated event; artifact creation under existing spines is the fast, template-driven path.\n\nRejected alternative — \"flexible spine wizard\" that lets users define new spines freely: Rejected because spine count is constitutionally sealed (5, precedence-ordered); a wizard that treats spine-creation as routine would erode the one guarantee that makes cross-artifact routing predictable. The cost of friction here (occasionally asking \"are you sure this isn't already ARCH?\") is far lower than the cost of spine proliferation.\n\nRejected alternative — schema-only wizard (just fill frontmatter fields, no classifier logic): Rejected because it would produce syntactically valid but semantically wrong core_spine assignments — the actual failure mode CSPS has hit historically (K=2 catches on closed-enum drift) came from authors filling fields correctly by form but incorrectly by meaning.\n\n▶ OPTIMAL NEXT STEP\n\nAction: Decide the wizard's delivery form — a CLI prompt sequence (pnpm spine:new), a Claude Code skill (like core-spine-expert but generative), or a standalone web form — before building the classifier logic | Unlocks: the classifier engine (Step 2) is the same regardless of delivery form, so this choice only affects the UI shell, but it determines whether validators wire in as pre-commit hooks (CLI) or as an async check (web form) | Why now: you're defining the wizard's steps in the abstract — the concrete build can't start until delivery form is fixed, and that's a cheap decision to make now versus mid-build."}]},"uuid":"c313f043-3309-4e6a-b576-484512a45ba2","timestamp":"2026-07-19T15:15:04.048Z","permissionMode":"acceptEdits","origin":{"kind":"human"},"promptSource":"sdk","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem","sessionId":"c249d411-23b2-46c5-9695-ddbaf884b7de","version":"2.1.210","gitBranch":"main","slug":"mutable-dazzling-blanket"}

Insight: \"the wizard's FIRST JOB is REFUSAL — structurally incapable of creating a 6th spine or reordering precedence. That constraint IS the product.\"\n- Step 1 DEFINE WHAT A SPINE IS (data model): a governance DOMAIN with a primary concern (governs-HOW-built / WHAT-built-on / AI-behavior / operations / standards-met), a sealed L1 doctrine file (changes = re-grounding event, not routine edit), an L2 domain layer, a fixed precedence rank (1-5, not per-spine assignable). MOST \"I need a new spine\" = \"I need a new L2 domain under an existing spine\" (the single most common failure). Only if genuinely orthogonal to all 5 → escalate to Governor (spine count is sealed). Silent cross-spine artifacts cause single-source-navigation failures; force declaration at creation (cheapest).\n- Step 5 VALIDATORS ATTACHED ATOMICALLY (Five-Surface Engraving): corespine-layer-compliance (core_spine ∈ canonical 5) + nothing-stands-alone-audit (schema_anchor present, no orphan) + template-citation-on-creation. A file without registered validator hooks EXISTS-but-not-ACTIVE (the most common failure the wizard exists to prevent).\n- Step 6 CLOSE WITH ACTIVATION PROOF not creation-confirmation: planted-violation test (does misclassifying core_spine get caught?) + positive-path confirm (correct one passes verify). DONE = wired+called+verified, not authored.\n- DECISION LEDGER — chosen: classifier-first, defaults to \"you probably don't need a new spine\", new-spine = rare Governor-gated event; artifact-under-existing-spine = fast template path. Refusal-as-feature. Mirrors our consolidation gate but sharper.\n- **SEALED count** (5 spines, precedence-fixed) vs our open corespine count — do WE want a sealed, bounded, precedence-ordered set of top-level corespines?
