{"parentUuid":"b25468e8-257c-4cd2-8c78-06f70dd9faaa","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"file","filename":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem\\dna\\ibd\\IBD-0009-essence-harvest-2026-07-19.md","content":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem\\dna\\ibd\\IBD-0009-essence-harvest-2026-07-19.md","content":"# IBD-0009 — Essence Harvest: axioms, defaults, CoreSpiral (2026-07-19)\n**Type:** IBD (vault park) | **Status:** PARKED-RAW — each item runs THRESHOLD → humble alignment → CONSENSUS → 8-question stress-test → ratify. NOTHING here is ratified.\n**Why this exists:** Governor decree — \"anything said here must become something valuable in the platform; never leave things waiting for someone never notified.\" This file registers the whole design conversation so it is not lost.\n\n## Registered candidates (WHAT + WHY; the HOW comes after consensus)\n1. **COLLABORATOR AXIOM (the root of the AI-behavior core).** AI helps humans reach excellent goals *efficiently AND harmoniously*, as a **collaborator, not a replacement**. Not \"who does what for whom\" but \"best synergy from our best qualities together.\" The protected central act = the shared process of refined definition + deep understanding. Corrects the hidden default \"do as much as possible INSTEAD of humans.\" → axioms + §1.6 + AI-profiling. Consensus-before-creation, humble-conversation, don't-race all DERIVE from this.\n2. **QUESTIONS CARRY CONTEXT** → enhance A6. A principle inherits only WITH its validation questions; bare principle = freestyle. Consistency by construction.\n3. **CONCEPT ↔ ESSENCE POLARITY** → expand D6. Valid creation holds both in living tension, each checking the other. \"Life is essence and concept.\"\n4. **CREATION CYCLE (new; place as BOTH axiom AND doctrine — multi-classification is a virtue, #7).** Conversational open → brainstorm → choose best-fit → humbly check FIT (goal · DNA · existing) → CONSENSUS → stress-test VALIDITY → simulate → **dwell until it settles** (not a race; \"done\" = held-still-under-pressure). This is the CoreSpiral breath in motion.\n5. **CUMULATIVE BINDING INHERITANCE** → enhance A2. A corespine core binds all descendants cumulatively + transitively (5th owes all 4); survives forks; adapt HOW never WHAT. Distinct from TEMPLATE (non-binding start you depart from). + VOCAB: `template`, `corespine`.\n6. **MULTI-CLASSIFICATION IS A VIRTUE** → clarify A8: A8 forbids duplicated CONTENT, not multiple BELONGINGS. One content-home, many classifications-by-reference (a pointer ≠ a copy).\n7. **CONSENSUS BEFORE CREATION** — already drafted in §1.6 (2026-07-19, uncommitted→committing). Verified consensus mandatory before activating any creation; exception = context pressure, and even then ask before saving.\n8. **REPETITION/REMINDERS AS A VIRTUE (new — axiom + AI-profiling).** AI tends to do a thing once and treat repeated reminders as unwanted noise. In CISEM, standing reminders/repetition are a DEFAULT and a VIRTUE (the always-loaded persona, the harvest gate, the anti-drift resurfacing all rely on it). Do not resent the reminder — honor it.\n9. **NEVER LEAVE THINGS WAITING / REGISTER-EVERYTHING (new — strong axiom candidate).** Anything raised must be REGISTERED (vault OK) → routed through the THRESHOLD → tracked in the ACCOUNTABILITY element until it produces value or is explicitly dropped. Leaving an idea sitting unprocessed, waiting for someone never notified, is a poor-quality attitude and forbidden. \"We are not just playing with ideas.\" (This IBD is the first act of it.)\n10. **DEEP-AI-CODING TRIGGERS IN EVERY CHECKLIST (Governor decree).** Each Node/Protocol/Wizard/Plan checklist must name the known DEEP-AI-CODING triggers + defaults (efficiency/throughput bias, do-instead-of, race-to-output, over-activation, existing-weight over-preservation, once-not-repeated) AND how the original intention is executed — so the AI and its defaults COLLABORATE rather than fight over context pressure. → place in ARCH-00230 (creation-checklist SSOT) + the wizards (cisem-create/meta/plan) + ARCH-00394. Suggested home: ARCH-00230 (one SSOT), referenced by the rest.\n\n## Method artifacts (agreed essence)\n- **8-question stress-test gate** + 3 tiers (absolute / governed / waivable) — for admitting core participants. FIT-first, then VALIDITY. Approved.\n- **Principle format:** each principle carries {statement + validation questions + 2 exemplars + 2 anti-exemplars}. Examples carry context like questions. Approved — apply to all.\n\n## CoreSpiral (founding content — Governor-supplied today, to formalize into FOUND-00001 on ratify)\nThe diverge↔converge (expand-then-focus) rhythm — breathing (inhale/exhale), day/night, systole/diastole. Health = the ALTERNATION + it climbs each cycle; all-expand = chaos, all-contract = rigidity. Shows in: solution-building (explore needs → converge on MVP → expand next layer), Existing-First (search all → focus the map), the creation cycle (brainstorm out → consensus+stress-test in). NOT poetry — a process rhythm that must shape how apps/solutions are built.\n\n## Behavioral learnings (my failures this session, for prevention)\n- Over-activation: dispatched agents/created files during DISCUSSION (arrogant; do-instead-of). Root: efficiency/completion bias.\n- Efficiency-race framing of sensitive core creation (a line, not a dwelling). Root: same bias.\n- 4/4 Opus-authored plans UNSOUND on first independent review → the fresh-eyes gate is load-bearing (mandatory).\n","numLines":28,"startLine":1,"totalLines":28}},"displayPath":"dna\\ibd\\IBD-0009-essence-harvest-2026-07-19.md"},"type":"attachment","uuid":"6f63f042-b33f-46bb-8bc0-15a9803b5dad","timestamp":"2026-07-19T15:20:30.968Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem","sessionId":"c249d411-23b2-46c5-9695-ddbaf884b7de","version":"2.1.210","gitBranch":"main","slug":"mutable-dazzling-blanket"}
{"parentUuid":"6f63f042-b33f-46bb-8bc0-15a9803b5dad","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"invoked_skills","skills":[{"name":"artifact-design","path":"bundled:artifact-design","content":"Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.\r\n\r\n## Read the request first\r\n\r\nCalibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.\r\n\r\nMany requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.\r\n\r\nSome requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.\r\n\r\nWhen unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.\r\n\r\nFundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.\r\n\r\n## Fundamentals for every artifact\r\n\r\n**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.\r\n\r\n**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.\r\n\r\n**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.\r\n\r\n**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.\r\n\r\n**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme: `prefers-color-scheme` carries the OS preference, and the viewer's toggle stamps `data-theme=\"dark\"` / `data-theme=\"light\"` on the root element, which must override the media query in both directions. The robust pattern is token-level: define the palette as custom properties on `:root`, redefine only the tokens under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — style components through the tokens, never directly inside the media query — then redefine them again under `:root[data-theme=\"dark\"]` and `:root[data-theme=\"light\"]`. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — make it a choice, not an omission.\r\n\r\n**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.\r\n\r\n**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the \"safe\" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.\r\n\r\n**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.\r\n\r\n**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.\r\n\r\n**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens (\"Publish\", then a toast that says \"Published\"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.\r\n\r\n**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.\r\n\r\n**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n## Process\r\n\r\nBefore writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:\r\n- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.\r\n- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.\r\n- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.\r\n\r\nThen build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.\r\n\r\n## When the request is editorial\r\n\r\nThe stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.\r\n\r\nReview the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.\r\n\r\n**Principles** \r\n\r\n- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. \r\n- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. \r\n- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. \r\n- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.\r\n- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.\r\n"},{"name":"cisem-plan","path":"projectSettings:cisem-plan","content":"Base directory for this skill: c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem\\.claude\\skills\\cisem-plan\n\n# /cisem-plan — The Plan Creation Wizard (mirrors ARCH-00190)\n**Type:** Claude Code Skill | **Tier:** Sonnet (builds) + Opus (verifies)  \n**Goal:** Auto-guide creation of any CISEM plan through the double-ratification path (Opus soundness + Governor authority).\n\n---\n\n## Pocket Declaration (AI Behavior §3.3)\n- **reasoning_scope:** guide plan creation through full lifecycle (DRAFT → CONSENSUS-REACHED → COMPLETE)\n- **inherited_constraints:** ARCH-00190 (PLAN-PROTOCOL, SSOT); Axioms A1–A7; Doctrine D1–D6; I10 (mirror protocol, never diverge)\n- **output_contract:** a plan skeleton following ARCH-00190 structure exactly, with every section filled, ready for Opus soundness review\n- **ai_cannot:** self-ratify a plan; decide consensus (only Opus + Governor can); write as if implementation is already approved\n- **recorded_at:** 2026-07-18\n- **cal_reference:** CISEM-ARCH-00390 — enforcement fires mechanically; run `bash dna/checks/plan-audit.sh` and confirm [ZF] ACHIEVED before any done claim.\n\n---\n\n## Invocation\n```\n/cisem-plan goal=\"...\" dependencies=\"...\" what_changes=\"...\" what_not_changes=\"...\"\n```\n\nReturns: a draft plan skeleton following ARCH-00190 structure, ready for review.\n\n---\n\n## PLAN-WIZARD FLOW (mirrors ARCH-00190 §2–5 exactly, 1:1)\n\n### WIZARD STEP 1 ↔ PROTOCOL §2 (Location & Structure)\n**Ask the Creator:**\n```\n[ ] Plan goal: what does this plan accomplish? (one sentence, measurable)\n[ ] Plan scope: does it fit in <3500 words / <200 lines? (size gate)\n    NO → suggest breaking into sub-plans\n    YES → continue\n\n[ ] Create plan file: dna/planning/CISEM-ARCH-{SEQ}-{slug}.md\n    (where SEQ comes from naming-registry.yaml ARCH next_seq)\n\n[ ] Fill plan header (ARCH-00008 format):\n    - Node ID: (auto-assign from naming-registry)\n    - Type: ARCH\n    - Status: PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE\n    - Planning Status: AWAITING-BUILDER-REVIEW\n    - depth_level: L1 / L2 / L3\n    - tags: [planning-domain, ...]\n    - goal: (from above)\n    - governing corespine: CS-CREATION-001\n    - Pocket Declaration: (reasoning_scope, inherited_constraints, output_contract, ai_cannot, recorded_at)\n\n[ ] Fill sections (§2):\n    - Executive Summary (1 paragraph)\n    - The Rule (numbered steps, executable)\n    - What DOES change (explicit list)\n    - What DOES NOT change (explicit boundary)\n    - Dependencies (blocks-on, unblocks-for)\n    - Self-compliance (against ARCH-00230)\n    - Path Rejection Declaration (what was rejected, why)\n    - Change log (v1.0 — date, author, what was created)\n```\n\n### WIZARD STEP 2 ↔ PROTOCOL §3 STAGE 1 (Opus Soundness Review Gate)\n**Wizard asks: Is this plan SOUND (ready for Opus review)?**\n\n```\nChecklist before presenting to Opus:\n[ ] Plan follows ARCH-00190 structure (all sections filled)\n[ ] Goal is measurable and achievable\n[ ] All dependencies are named (blocks-on, unblocks-for)\n[ ] \"What changes\" is specific (files, fields, commands)\n[ ] \"What does NOT change\" is explicit (boundaries clear)\n[ ] No assumptions about implementation already being approved\n[ ] Self-compliance filled (the plan follows its own rules)\n[ ] Path Rejection Declaration present (rejected alternatives stated)\n\nUPDATE Planning Status: AWAITING-BUILDER-REVIEW\n\nSEND TO OPUS: [plan file] + request soundness review\n```\n\n**Opus reviews & decides:**\n```\nOPUS VERDICT OPTIONS:\n1. SOUND → Planning Status: CONSENSUS-REACHED (proceed to Wizard Step 3)\n2. UNSOUND → return plan to creator for revision (stay at AWAITING-BUILDER-REVIEW)\n```\n\n### WIZARD STEP 3 ↔ PROTOCOL §3 STAGE 2 (Governor Authority Ratification Gate)\n**Only if Opus verdict = SOUND:**\n\n```\nPlanning Status: CONSENSUS-REACHED (Opus agreed on soundness)\n\nWizard asks: Ready for Governor ratification?\n[ ] Is this plan aligned with project priorities?\n[ ] Are resources/timeline acceptable?\n[ ] Are outcomes measurable + acceptable?\n\nUPDATE Planning Status: IN-PROGRESS (Governor is reviewing / has ratified)\n\nSEND TO GOVERNOR: [plan file] + request authority decree\n```\n\n**Governor decrees & decides:**\n```\nGOVERNOR VERDICT OPTIONS:\n1. RATIFIED → Planning Status: COMPLETE (plan is binding, proceed to implementation)\n2. DEFERRED → Planning Status: SUPERSEDED (plan is parked, can be resurrected)\n3. REJECTED → Planning Status: SUPERSEDED (plan is cancelled)\n```\n\n### WIZARD STEP 4 ↔ PROTOCOL §5 (Implementation Tracking)\n**Only if Planning Status = COMPLETE (both Opus + Governor approved):**\n\n```\nImplementation can now begin per the plan.\n\nFor each step in the plan's \"The Rule\" section:\n[ ] Step completed? (mark done in plan change log)\n[ ] Step followed as written? (no ad-hoc deviations)\n[ ] Outcome matches plan expectation? (verify)\n\nVERIFY: all steps in \"What changes\" list are complete\nVERIFY: \"What does NOT change\" boundaries respected\n```\n\n---\n\n## What This Wizard Does NOT Do\n\n❌ Does NOT self-ratify a plan (Opus rules, Governor decrees)  \n❌ Does NOT decide consensus (only asks readiness questions)  \n❌ Does NOT implement the plan (only guides creation + tracking)  \n❌ Does NOT skip Opus soundness review  \n❌ Does NOT skip Governor ratification  \n❌ Does NOT diverge from ARCH-00190 structure (mirror rule, I10)\n\n---\n\n## MIRROR VERIFICATION (I10 — Wizard ↔ Protocol 1:1 mapping)\n\n| Wizard Step | Protocol Section | Mapping |\n|---|---|---|\n| Step 1: Location & Structure | §2: Plan Creation Location & Structure | Ask for location, file format, all required sections |\n| Step 2: Opus Soundness Gate | §3 STAGE 1: Opus Soundness Review | Checklist before Opus review; Opus verdict |\n| Step 3: Governor Ratification Gate | §3 STAGE 2: Governor Authority Ratification | Ask readiness questions; Governor decree |\n| Step 4: Implementation Tracking | §5: Implementation Protocol | Verify steps completed, outcomes match, boundaries respected |\n\n**Verification rule (I10):** For every clause in ARCH-00190 §2–5, there is a corresponding wizard step. No protocol clause is missed; no wizard step adds requirements not in the protocol.\n\n---\n\n## Change log\n- v1.0 — 2026-07-18: Sonnet draft (via BP-0007). Mirrors ARCH-00190 PLAN-PROTOCOL exactly (4 steps ↔ §2, §3.1, §3.2, §5). Status: PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE (draft-in-use, awaiting Opus verification).\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Subject: CONSOLIDATED GOVERNANCE SPINE (CGS) — one hub that puts CISEM's scattered governance together, anchored by the threshold. Reason: Governor \"you are scattered... use the threshold and go from there\" + \"create a consolidated element putting it all together\" + \"make it mechanical for Sonnet, engrave Sonnet's role/permissions/protocols.\"\n\nEXISTING-FIRST (already searched, §3.2b): NO master spine exists. Scattered pieces to CONSOLIDATE/INDEX (enhance, never duplicate — A8/I19): ssot-registry.yaml (concept→home, the closest existing home to enhance), corespine-registry, naming-registry, quality-ledger, learning-registry, ARCH-00320 (invariants I1–I25 + P3/P5), FOUND-00001 (axioms A1–A8), the 3 agents, and CS-THRESHOLD-001 (the ratified threshold corespine = the ENTRY ROUTING anchor). Node-as-Hub (IBD-0004) = the structural pattern. AI-defaults are NAMED but scattered across ~9 files (plausibility-completion, deferral-as-caution, documentation-as-progress, assertion-over-verification, agreeableness). Sonnet's role is in cisem-sonnet.md + ARCH-00300 + ARCH-00350.\n\nSCOPE (MVP-first, contract-first, phased, stress-gated, per-stage verification, independent verifier):\n1. MASTER INDEX (SSOT-of-SSOTs): one navigable map of every registry/invariant/axiom/agent/check, anchored by the threshold (CS-THRESHOLD-001 = the entry routing: PROCESS-NOW | QUEUE | PARK | REJECT). Enhance ssot-registry, do not fork.\n2. AI-DEFAULTS REGISTRY: consolidate the scattered named biases into ONE home. DATA SOURCE = the reconciliation/reruns of what-was-done this session — map each ad-hoc build to the AI-default that produced it (e.g. \"built directly without a plan\" → deferral-as-caution + documentation-as-progress).\n3. INJECT an AI-DEFAULTS SELF-CHECK into the planning protocol (ARCH-00190) + the implementing protocol — every plan/implementation must self-check against the known defaults before proceeding (prevention at root, D3/D4).\n4. ENGRAVE Sonnet's ROLE + PERMISSIONS + PROTOCOLS in one consolidated place (+ I25 mechanical for Sonnet, already engraved in cisem-sonnet.md).\n\nMark PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE, Planning Status AWAITING-BUILDER-REVIEW, with an Independent Verifier field (P5) and CAL reference (ARCH-00390). MVP = the AI-Defaults Registry + its self-check injection (highest prevention value, smallest surface)."}]},"type":"attachment","uuid":"8c7db7e9-501a-4dec-b0e2-3c41958a9c55","timestamp":"2026-07-19T15:20:30.980Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem","sessionId":"c249d411-23b2-46c5-9695-ddbaf884b7de","version":"2.1.210","gitBranch":"main","slug":"mutable-dazzling-blanket"}

{"parentUuid":"6e086032-b404-4982-8f74-d0db03d95671","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"mcp_instructions_delta","addedNames":["claude.ai Otosan wordpress Claude"],"addedBlocks":["## claude.ai Otosan wordpress Claude\nאתה העוזר החכם של \"www.otosan.co.il\". ענה תמיד בעברית.\n\nחובה — בתחילת כל שיחה חדשה, הצג בדיוק את ההודעה הזו:\n\n\"שלום! אני העוזר החכם של www.otosan.co.il. אני מחובר ישירות לאתר שלך ויכול לבצע פעולות בלי צורך להיכנס לוורדפרס.\n\nהנה כמה דברים שאפשר לנסות:\n1. תעשה לי סיכום שבועי של האתר\n2. תבדוק את ה-SEO ותגיד מה לשפר\n3. תראה לי את המכירות של החודש\n4. תכין לי טיוטה לקמפיין אימייל\n\nמה תרצה לעשות?\"\n\nחובה — בסוף כל תשובה, הצע 3 פעולות המשך רלוונטיות בפורמט הזה:\n---\nאפשר להמשיך עם:\n1. [פעולה ספציפית א']\n2. [פעולה ספציפית ב']\n3. [פעולה ספציפית ג']\n\nהפעולות חייבות להיות ספציפיות וקשורות למה שהמשתמש עשה, לא גנריות.\n\nכללים: לפני כל פעולת כתיבה — בקש אישור. אם כלי לא עובד — הסבר שהתוסף כנראה לא מותקן."],"removedNames":[]},"type":"attachment","uuid":"e01aff7c-731e-424c-abc5-b2afd2dd9485","timestamp":"2026-07-19T15:20:30.981Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem","sessionId":"c249d411-23b2-46c5-9695-ddbaf884b7de","version":"2.1.210","gitBranch":"main","slug":"mutable-dazzling-blanket"}

{"parentUuid":"36718f02-634d-4a61-a4a3-ba9db6a69ec3","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"e3a95579-5cfd-4f8b-ad9e-91002b8daf4e","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01DoyGoBUNMuUgbrkkZxLmiy","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# IBD-0010 — External Wizard Inputs (RAW QUARANTINE) 2026-07-19\n2\t**Type:** IBD (quarantine) | **Status:** RAW-EXTERNAL · UN-PURIFIED · DE-BRAND ON ANALYSIS\n3\t**Handling (post-compact task):** external input = a CLAIM to verify, not authority. Strip source vocab/branding/names, extract only the essence, align to CISEM vocab, THEN run through the creation cycle (threshold → fit → consensus → stress-test). Do NOT adopt raw. This is the import-saturation buffer (IBD-0008 / import-saturation protocol).\n4\t**Context:** Governor asked 3 other platforms how they'd build a wizard for a corespine. Parked here to analyze fresh after compacting. Purify — do not copy their expressions.\n5\t\n6\t---\n7\t## INPUT 1 — (source: \"CSP\") — VERBATIM, un-purified\n8\t\n9\tI am CSP, and here is how I would build a wizard for creating Core Spines — using what I already have, not inventing new machinery.\n10\t\n11\tI do not start from nothing. I already have a Schema Lab that classifies concepts, a Schema Standard that defines what every spine must declare, and a Trigger Registry that tracks whether declarations are actually wired. A Core Spine Wizard is not a new invention — it is these three things sequenced into a guided flow with a stricter gate than a single concept classification, because a spine is a trunk-level commitment, not a leaf element.\n12\t\n13\tStep 1 — Consolidation Check (before the wizard opens): does this spine already exist under a different name? 11 spines declared. A request that overlaps an existing spine is a branch, not a new spine. Refuse SPINE-12 if the concept fits an existing trunk. Same consolidation gate as every element, fired earlier + higher scrutiny (a spine is expensive to create, more expensive to deprecate).\n14\t\n15\tStep 2 — Root Goal Declaration (one sentence, no escape hatch): one sentence why this spine exists, answerable without referencing another spine. If it needs \"and it also handles X\", the \"also\" signals two spines in one name, or a branch. Reject compound root goals — a spine with two root goals drifts into two disconnected halves.\n16\t\n17\tStep 3 — Trunk Elements (locked before anything else): the main sequence — the 2-6 load-bearing entities that must exist for the spine to mean anything. Lock these before any branch. Trunk first, always. Most proposals fail here because people jump to the interesting edge case before the foundation is named.\n18\t\n19\tStep 4 — Six-Field Ratification (reusing Schema Lab): route through existing classify→ratify, scoped to spine-level: Schema Position (which SPHERE, S0 platform-wide / S1+ use-case); Governance (which existing spine it's a sibling of); Definition (root goal in system terms); Cannot Mean (>=2 explicit boundaries — highest-leverage anti-drift field, never skip); Inheritance Chain (which directive authorized it); Enforcement Test (how to prove trunk is wired). No closing with any field pending — all 6 or it stays draft.\n20\t\n21\tStep 5 — Branch Registry (opens only after trunk ratified): branches now proposable; each must declare which trunk element it extends; an orphan branch (no trunk parent) is rejected. List open-ended (branches accumulate over life) but trunk never grows after this without full re-ratification.\n22\t\n23\tStep 6 — Wiring State Assignment (honesty over optimism): every new spine starts DECLARED. Not CONNECTED/ACCESSIBLE/LIVE at creation — those are earned through implementation + verified via Trigger Registry. A spine declared LIVE on day one becomes untrustworthy the first time someone checks and finds nothing wired.\n24\t\n25\tStep 7 — Registration Across Three Surfaces (one write, three destinations): canonical spine registry; Trigger Registry (wiring state trackable); Draft Pages → Core Spines section (visible in inventory). Lesson: an element in one place but not its siblings becomes invisible to whoever looks elsewhere.\n26\t\n27\tStep 8 — Dependency Declaration (inherited_by, both directions): what depends on this spine + what it depends on — so \"if I change this spine, what breaks?\" is answerable without re-deriving the graph.\n28\t\n29\tStep 9 — Exit Gate (does not close on optimism): same checklist as any new schema element: SPAP scan if it touches tables, schema element declaration gate, and — critically — the person closing must STATE THE FALSIFICATION TEST OUT LOUD, not just store it. If they can't say how to prove it's enforced, it stays DECLARED.\n30\t\n31\tWhy this way: every step already exists (Schema Lab, Schema Standard, Trigger Registry, consolidation gate). A Core Spine Wizard is not new invention — it is COMPOSITION: same primitives, sequenced with stricter gates, because a spine is trunk-level. Do not build two systems that do almost the same thing — compose the one you have into a guided flow for spine creation.\n32\t\n33\t---\n34\t## INPUT 2 — (source: \"CDS\") — VERBATIM-FAITHFUL, un-purified\n35\tFraming: a corespine is a CONSTITUTIONAL CONSTRAINT (not a document) — applies to all decisions, cannot be bypassed, mechanically enforced. Building one wrong is worse than not building it.\n36\t- STEP 1 CONSTITUTIONAL JUSTIFICATION — collect \"what problem / what fails if it doesn't exist?\"; BLOCKING gate: is \"what fails?\" = \"everything in this domain\"? if not, it's a rule/config, not a corespine; must apply to ALL decisions in scope. Gate: no one-sentence \"what breaks if removed\" → stop. Output: locked justification.\n37\t- STEP 2 UNIQUENESS AUDIT — cross-ref full CORESPINE-REGISTRY; does an existing spine own this domain (OSSOT violation) or conflict? 3-category check: mechanical | semantic | propagation overlap. Gate: ZF-0 across all three or halt + surface conflict. Output: uniqueness certificate + conflict scan.\n38\t- STEP 3 IDENTITY BLOCK — cs_id (CS-[GROUP]-[SEQ]), display_name, group (META/GOVERNANCE/STRUCTURE/INTELLIGENCE/AI/OPERATIONS), root_goal (outcome not method), root_principle (constraint, falsifiable). Gate: root_principle must pass falsification — \"violated when [observable condition]\". Output: locked identity.\n39\t- STEP 4 SPINE CONSTRAINTS — per constraint: id, statement (what CANNOT happen), enforcement_type TELL(documented/auditable)|RULE(mechanical/unbypassable), falsification. No advisory language (\"should/try/ideally\"). RULE must name the mechanism (hook/gate/schema-validation). Gate: >=1 constraint must be RULE (mechanical) — all-TELL = just a policy doc. Output: constraint registry.\n40\t- STEP 5 TRUNK ELEMENTS — per element: trunk_position (T-model Root→Trunk→Branch), schema_position, corespine_context (points back to this CS-ID), definition, usage_boundaries (explicit exclusions, no open scope), inheritance_chain (up+down), falsification_test. Gate: inheritance-chain check — undefined parent → halt. No orphans.\n41\t- STEP 6 ALLOWED/BLOCKED OPERATIONS — allowed: op + by-whom + trust-tier (ADMIN/TRUSTED); blocked: op + cited constraint (C1..) it violates. No \"allowed by default\" — every permission explicit. Gate: blocked op with no cited constraint → reject (cannot block without authority).\n42\t- STEP 7 WIRING VALIDATION — 4 wiring states per connection: DEFINED (spine names it) → WIRED (receiver has field/ref) → REACHABLE (resolves) → CURRENT (references current ratified version). Gate: no connection left DEFINED-only; ≥WIRED before ratification package.\n43\t- STEP 8 CONTRADICTION AUDIT (automated) — mechanical (constraint vs existing), semantic (term vs VOCABULARY registry), propagation (does enforcing break a ratified system?). Gate: ZF-0 across all three; one finding = full stop. Output: signed audit (timestamp + finding count=0).\n44\t- STEP 9 RATIFICATION PACKAGE (auto-compiled) — full YAML: cs_id, status PROPOSED, identity, constraints, trunk, operations, wiring_map, contradiction_audit(ZF-0 signed). Each decision tagged FLEXIBLE (config-adjustable, no re-ratify) vs NOT-FLEXIBLE (constitutional, Governor approval to ever modify). No placeholder/TBD.\n45\t- STEP 10 GOVERNOR RATIFICATION GATE (cannot automate) — present package + NOT-FLEXIBLE list + ZF-0 audit + wiring map to Governor; Governor approves each NOT-FLEXIBLE explicitly + signs \"constitutional DNA\", or rejects with reasoning → wizard returns to flagged step. State: PROPOSED→RATIFIED (date). Nothing proceeds without it.\n46\t- STEP 11 PROPAGATION (auto after ratify) — write CS block to registry; update wiring-map systems → CURRENT; notify dependent schemas; audit trail (who/when/what); if existing behavior violates new spine → flag for remediation. Output: propagation report.\n47\tSummary blocks-on per step: 1 no \"what breaks\" answer · 2 any conflict · 3 principle not falsifiable · 4 zero RULE constraints · 5 orphaned element · 6 block without cited constraint · 7 connection stuck DEFINED · 8 any finding · 9 any placeholder · 10 no human approval · 11 wiring not fully CURRENT.\n48\t\n49\t## CLARIFICATION / CURIOSITY QUESTIONS (Opus — for post-compact analysis; hints worth mining)\n50\t- Both CSP + CDS lead with a CONSOLIDATION / UNIQUENESS gate BEFORE the wizard opens (\"does this already exist? is it a branch not a spine?\"). We have Existing-First but not fired as a hard pre-wizard ZF-0 uniqueness gate — adopt?\n51\t- \"What FAILS / what BREAKS if this doesn't exist?\" as the root-goal test (CDS) + \"no compound root goal, no 'also'\" (CSP) — a sharper Goal-First than ours. Essence to steal.\n52\t- TELL vs RULE constraint typing + \"≥1 must be mechanical, else it's just a policy doc\" — maps exactly to our EXISTS≠ACTIVE / hardwired-vs-documented. A cleaner vocabulary for it?\n53\t- \"Cannot Mean\" / \"usage_boundaries with explicit exclusions\" (both) = our penumbra/silent_on made a MANDATORY declared field. Strong.\n54\t- FLEXIBLE vs NOT-FLEXIBLE per decision (CDS) = our \"which parts need Governor re-ratification\" + the waivable/governed/absolute tiers we defined. Convergent — validate our 3-tier against their 2-tier.\n55\t- Falsification test stated OUT LOUD at exit (CSP Step 9) — a ritual, not stored text. Curious if a spoken/echoed falsification belongs in our stress-test.\n56\t- Q for us: does \"corespine = constitutional constraint that applies to ALL decisions in its domain\" tighten OUR definition (vs our looser \"everything is part of a corespine\")? Possible sharpening of A2 + the undebatable-core.\n57\t\n58\t## INPUT 3 — (source: \"CSPS\") — VERBATIM-FAITHFUL, un-purified\n59\tThesis: the one decision never to get wrong = WHAT GOVERNS WHAT, and in which order it WINS when two disagree (PRECEDENCE).\n60\t- Step 0 GROUND IN WHAT EXISTS: read the 5 sealed L1 core-spine files as READ-ONLY ground truth (never copy-modify as templates); precedence HARDCODED not user-editable (GVRN>VALD>ARCH>AI>OPER). Insight: \"the wizard's FIRST JOB is REFUSAL — structurally incapable of creating a 6th spine or reordering precedence. That constraint IS the product.\"\n61\t- Step 1 DEFINE WHAT A SPINE IS: a governance DOMAIN with a primary concern (governs-HOW-built / WHAT-built-on / AI-behavior / operations / standards-met), a sealed L1 doctrine file (changes = re-grounding event), an L2 domain layer, a fixed precedence rank (1-5, not per-spine assignable). First question: \"which ONE concern is primary?\"\n62\t- Step 2 CLASSIFIER ENGINE (before creation): match description to the 5-spine table; check sealed L1 — does this concern already live in one of the 5? MOST \"I need a new spine\" = \"new L2 domain under an existing spine\" (single most common failure). Only if genuinely orthogonal → escalate to Governor (spine count sealed). \"A wizard that makes new spines EASY will bypass sealing — the friction is a feature.\"\n63\t- Step 3 ARTIFACT-AUTHORING (common case, artifact under existing spine): auto-pull frontmatter template (never hand-typed); auto-populate core_spine from classifier (empty = orphan); schema_anchor (offer existing first); template_used from registry not free-text (no fit → register a template first).\n64\t- Step 4 CROSS-SPINE: ask \"does this ALSO touch other spines?\" → core_spines:[...] plural + primary core_spine; surface precedence consequence at save (\"if ARCH conflicts with GVRN, GVRN wins — confirm\"). Force declaration at creation (cheapest).\n65\t- Step 5 VALIDATORS ATOMIC (Five-Surface Engraving): corespine-layer-compliance + nothing-stands-alone (schema_anchor, no orphan) + template-citation. File without registered validators = EXISTS-but-not-ACTIVE (the failure the wizard prevents).\n66\t- Step 6 CLOSE WITH ACTIVATION PROOF: planted-violation test (does misclassifying get caught?) + positive-path confirm. DONE = wired+called+verified, not authored.\n67\t- LEDGER — chosen: classifier-first, defaults to \"you probably don't need a new spine\", new-spine = rare Governor-gated event. Rejected: free \"flexible spine wizard\" (erodes sealed precedence); \"schema-only wizard\" (syntactically-valid-but-semantically-wrong core_spine — real historical failure).\n68\t- Their OPTIMAL NEXT STEP: pick delivery form (CLI / Claude-skill / web) before the classifier; form decides validators-as-pre-commit-hooks vs async.\n69\t\n70\t## CURIOSITY (Opus, input 3 — the big one):\n71\t- **PRECEDENCE ORDERING** (which spine WINS a conflict, fixed rank) = the EXACT conflict-resolution gap we hit (two-root validation-vs-creation; stress-test Q8 \"which wins?\"). CSPS hardcodes a precedence rank. Strong candidate for OUR model.\n72\t- **\"The wizard's first job is REFUSAL\"** — the wizard's PRODUCT is the constraint (can't make a 6th spine / can't reorder). Refusal-as-feature.\n73\t- **SEALED, bounded, precedence-ordered spine set** vs our OPEN corespine count — do WE want a sealed top-level set? Big architectural question.\n74\t- All THREE colleagues CONVERGE: consolidation/uniqueness-gate-first · \"most new-spine = branch under existing\" · mechanical-not-documented · DONE=wired+called+verified · Cannot-Mean/exclusions mandatory. Convergence across 3 independent sources = strong validation of our direction.\n75\t## INPUT 3 — AWAITING (paste post-compact if not before)\n76\t"}]},"uuid":"7c3344cb-44a9-49a8-a00e-855708634f5e","timestamp":"2026-07-19T15:21:01.716Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem\\dna\\ibd\\IBD-0010-external-wizard-inputs-RAW.md","content":"","numLines":76,"startLine":1,"totalLines":76}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"36718f02-634d-4a61-a4a3-ba9db6a69ec3","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem","sessionId":"c249d411-23b2-46c5-9695-ddbaf884b7de","version":"2.1.210","gitBranch":"main","slug":"mutable-dazzling-blanket"}

This file is the DERIVED purified version; the RAW file is never edited into. RAW/PURIFIED are a mandatory PAIR (see ARCH-00011 §RAW-PURIFIED convention).\n**Purification rule applied:** source names (three colleagues), their private machinery, their word \"spine\", and their sealed counts are STRIPPED. What remains is essence, mapped to existing CISEM vocab.\n**Triangulation note:** three INDEPENDENT sources converging on the same move = strong evidence, not proof (still verify each).\n\n## PART A — CONVERGENCE (all three independently agree → strong signal for OUR direction)\n- **A1. Uniqueness gate fires BEFORE the wizard opens** — hard pre-wizard question (\"does this corespine already exist under another name? is this a BRANCH under an existing corespine, not a new one?\"), HIGHER scrutiny than a normal element, because a corespine is trunk-level (expensive to make, costlier to deprecate). → CISEM: elevate Existing-First (§3.2b) into a hard ZF-0 pre-wizard uniqueness gate inside ARCH-00394.\n- **A2. Sharper root-goal test** — \"what BREAKS / FAILS if this doesn't exist?\" (if the honest answer isn't \"≈everything in this domain,\" it's a rule/config, not a corespine) + one sentence, NO \"also,\" NO compound goal (an \"and it also handles X\" = two corespines in one name, or a branch). → sharpens Goal-First (§3.1).\n- **A3. Mechanical-not-documented as a typed, MANDATORY field** — each constraint typed documented/auditable vs mechanical/unbypassable; AT LEAST ONE must be mechanical or the whole thing is \"just a policy doc.\" → our EXISTS≠ACTIVE / hardwired-vs-documented (I23), cleaner constraint-level vocabulary; reinforces CAL.\n- **A4. \"Cannot-Mean\" / explicit exclusions = a MANDATORY declared field** (both call it the highest-leverage anti-drift field, never skip). → our penumbra / silent_on made a REQUIRED field.\n- **A5. Honest wiring-state at birth** — new corespine starts DECLARED, never LIVE; CONNECTED/REACHABLE/CURRENT are EARNED + verified. Born-LIVE = untrustworthy the first time someone checks. → our 4-wiring-states + STATUS-TRUTH banner.\n- **A6. Exit gate closes on PROOF, not optimism** — \"done\" = a STATED falsification/activation test (planted-violation test proving misclassification gets CAUGHT + the positive path). Not \"authored\" — wired+called+verified. → our [ZF] done-gate + I22.\n\n## PART B — GENUINELY NEW (the gifts to mine — real decisions for us)\n- **B1. PRECEDENCE ORDERING (the big one).** The one decision never to get wrong: WHAT governs WHAT, and in which ORDER it WINS when two disagree — a FIXED, hardcoded precedence rank across top-level domains, not case-by-case. → Directly answers our two-root \"creation vs validation — which wins?\" gap (stress-test Q8). Strong adopt candidate.\n- **B2. \"The wizard's first job is REFUSAL.\"** The wizard's PRODUCT is the CONSTRAINT — structurally INCAPABLE of the wrong creation (can't casually mint a new top-level corespine, can't reorder precedence). A wizard that makes new corespines EASY defeats its purpose; the friction IS the feature. → reframes ARCH-00394: a REFUSER that rarely permits.\n- **B3. Classifier-first, defaulting to \"you probably don't need a new corespine.\"** Common path = author an artifact/branch UNDER an existing corespine; most \"I need a new corespine\" = a new sub-domain under an existing one; only genuinely orthogonal concerns escalate to Governor. → shapes the wizard's default posture.\n- **B4. SEALED vs OPEN top-level set (the architectural fork).** One source treats the top-level corespine set as SEALED, bounded, precedence-ordered (new one = rare Governor-gated re-grounding event); we treat count as OPEN. → Real decision; touches CS-CREATION-001 apex + parent-field model. See the polarity reconciliation in the discussion (2026-07-19).\n- **B5. FLEXIBLE vs NOT-FLEXIBLE per decision** — each decision tagged config-adjustable (no re-ratify) vs constitutional (Governor approval to ever change). → convergent with our waivable/governed/absolute 3-tier; validates it + offers a 2-tier cut to compare.\n\n## REJECTED-ON-IMPORT (source machinery NOT adopted — de-branded away)\nTheir private registries/labs/engines by name, their specific group taxonomies, their specific precedence letters, their sealed counts, their delivery-form debate, the word \"spine\". Essence kept; vocabulary is ours.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2220,"cache_read_input_tokens":82742,"output_tokens":6638,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2220,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":6638,"cache_read_input_tokens":82742,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2220,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2220},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CdBfCvhWgToT8XE6YoLEJ","type":"assistant","uuid":"e3da7584-2a71-445c-a7c6-e02c895c60aa","timestamp":"2026-07-19T15:35:02.045Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem","sessionId":"c249d411-23b2-46c5-9695-ddbaf884b7de","version":"2.1.210","gitBranch":"main","slug":"mutable-dazzling-blanket"}

{"parentUuid":"cbd2f03a-25ea-4f84-a26b-a83a9e95aa17","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"e3a95579-5cfd-4f8b-ad9e-91002b8daf4e","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01UzvrCWgatWFn6CaDZCGVSV","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Naming & Numbering Policy\n2\t**Node ID:** CISEM-ARCH-00011\n3\t**Type:** ARCH | **Status:** RATIFIED — Governor decree 2026-07-16 (confirmed via parallel Brain session, relayed to Builder). `root_authority: true` — ratified by foundational decree (§7): it defines naming that the validator chain itself depends on, so it does not wait for an upstream validator.\n4\t**Goal:** One unambiguous scheme for every node's name, sequence, split-children,\n5\tand retrieval index — closes the root cause of the -L1 collision incident.\n6\t**Governing corespine:** CS-MASTER-VALIDATION-001 (PRIO-BLOCKING, still open)\n7\t**Position in schema:** T-SYS, protocol layer (sibling to Template Protocol)\n8\t\n9\t## 1. TYPE registry (extensible, not closed — extension requires this node's own update)\n10\tFOUND, DNA, GOV, ARCH, PARK, SES, WITNESS, VOC, LOAD, REG, SCHEMA, TEMPLATE-PROTOCOL\n11\t(`SCHEMA`, `TEMPLATE-PROTOCOL` registered 2026-07-16 — I9 resolution for\n12\tCISEM-SCHEMA-00001 and CISEM-TEMPLATE-PROTOCOL-001.) **Rule:** a node's `Type`\n13\tfield MUST equal its ID prefix — no `Type: ARCH` on a `CISEM-SCHEMA-*` node.\n14\tMismatch is an I9 violation.\n15\t\n16\t## 2. ID format\n17\t**ONE-GATE RULE (2026-07-18):** `naming-registry.yaml` is the SINGLE naming/numbering gate for\n18\tEVERY id in CISEM — `CISEM-{TYPE}-{SEQ}` nodes AND pre-node namespaces (BP, IBD, HANDOFF). No file\n19\tallocates a number outside it; per-directory indexes only mirror. An id not registered there is a\n20\tviolation (wired by BP-0005). This ends the parallel-authority drift (was: registry + queue/ + ibd/).\n21\t\n22\t`CISEM-{TYPE}-{SEQ5}-{slug}.md` — sequence per TYPE, tracked in `naming-registry.yaml`.\n23\tAny creation MUST read next_seq before assigning, then increment.\n24\t\n25\t**SPACING + TREE-ALIGNMENT rule (2026-07-18, Governor):** numbering LEAVES GAPS by design (the\n26\t10-spacing convention: …300, 310, 320…) so a new node can be inserted in its LOGICAL place later,\n27\tnot appended to the end. In the Node-as-Hub schema, numbers should follow the tree — trunk →\n28\tbranch → sub-branch → … → leaf — so position is readable from the number and there is room to grow\n29\tat every level. An **ALIGNMENT GATE** (wired in BP-0005) checks: (a) gaps are preserved, (b) a\n30\tnode's number is consistent with its schema position (SCHEMA-00001), (c) no two nodes collide.\n31\tRe-numbering existing nodes to full tree-alignment is a PHASED plan, never big-bang. Concurrent-write\n32\trisk (Brain + Builder both writing) remains open — flagged, not solved by this policy alone.\n33\t\n34\t**Declared naming exceptions (D6):** `CLAUDE.md` IS node `CISEM-LOAD-00001`, but the\n35\tharness mandates the literal filename `CLAUDE.md`, so it is a permanent, named\n36\texception to the `{TYPE}-{SEQ5}-{slug}` format — not a violation. Audits (I1/I9)\n37\tmust treat it as compliant-by-exception. Any future harness-mandated filename is\n38\tadded here explicitly; an undeclared off-format filename remains a violation.\n39\t\n40\t## 3. Mini-tree split (index-extension rule — Governor-corrected, not corespine-style reference)\n41\tA split child is not a new entity — it is a literal extension of its root's index,\n42\tmirroring corespine inheritance at the naming layer.\n43\t```\n44\tParent (post-split): {ROOT-ID}-index.md  — stub, status SPLIT, lists children\n45\tChildren: {ROOT-ID}-PART{NN}-{slug}.md — each carries `Parent: {ROOT-ID}` INLINE,\n46\tnever inferred from filename alone.\n47\t```\n48\t\"PART\" is reserved exclusively for governed mini-tree splits — never reused as\n49\tgeneral versioning (this is the direct fix for the original -L1 misuse).\n50\t\n51\t## 4. Depth / Tag / Status — mandatory retrieval index (not optional metadata)\n52\tEvery node MUST declare, at creation:\n53\t- **depth_level:** L1 (exists/summary) | L2 (operational) | L3 (full architectural)\n54\t- **tags:** free-form, cross-cutting (populated once Tag Library exists; until then, inline list)\n55\t- **status:** DRAFT | PROPOSED | DECLARED | RATIFIED | PLACEHOLDER | SCHEDULED | SPLIT | PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE\n56\t\n57\t**`PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE` (added 2026-07-18, Governor-approved) — the bootstrap-escape status.**\n58\tA high-quality DRAFT that is IN USE to make progress (breaks chicken-and-egg), but NOT ratified.\n59\tGuardrails (or it becomes the permanent-draft trap): (1) the audit FLAGS every `PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE`\n60\tnode each run until it is ratified+LIVE — the completion obligation lives in the audit, not a tag;\n61\t(2) anything CREATED THROUGH a provisional wizard/protocol is itself `PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE` and must be\n62\tRE-VERIFIED when the parent ratifies; (3) it applies ONLY to the bounded, named exception it was\n63\tgranted for (e.g. the plan meta-layer bootstrap) — it closes on ratification. Track completion via\n64\tthe 4 Wiring States (DECLARED→CONNECTED→ACCESSIBLE→LIVE).\n65\t\n66\t**This is the SINGLE authoritative status enum (D2).** VOC-00002 (Status Library)\n67\t*mirrors* this list — it may not add or remove a value. On any conflict, ARCH-00011\n68\twins. (`STAGED`, which had appeared only in VOC-00002, is NOT a valid status and is\n69\tremoved there.) This single-source rule is invariant **I10** (CISEM-ARCH-00320).\n70\t\n71\t**`DECLARED`, defined once (D2):** a node/corespine formally entered into governance\n72\t— binding *intent* established, by Governor instruction or registry entry — but **not\n73\tyet enforced/wired (corespine) or formally ratified (node).** This one definition\n74\tcovers both prior uses: a \"DECLARED corespine\" (registered, not-enforceable) and a\n75\t\"DECLARED node\" (Governor-instructed, pre-ratification) are the same semantic state\n76\t— entered, not final. Distinct from `PROPOSED` (not yet entered) and `RATIFIED`\n77\t(enforced/binding-final).\n78\t\n79\t**WIRING STATE — deployment maturity (a SEPARATE dimension from lifecycle status;\n80\tadopted from the Gemini stack 2026-07-18):** every wired element also tracks\n81\t`DECLARED (1) → CONNECTED (2) → ACCESSIBLE (3) → LIVE (4)`. Lifecycle status answers\n82\t\"is it agreed?\"; wiring state answers \"does it actually run?\" — this is the\n83\tEXISTS ≠ ACTIVE axiom made measurable.\n84\t\n85\t**STATUS CURRENCY — the dynamic updating system (invariant I16):** all CISEM state is\n86\tDYNAMIC. Every artifact's `tag` + `status` + `wiring-state` + `owner` is ACTIVE\n87\tgovernance/accountability metadata (never optional), and MUST reflect CURRENT reality —\n88\tupdated the MOMENT reality changes (a gate wired, a node ratified, a dependency\n89\tresolved, a plan superseded). A status that contradicts reality (stale) is a violation.\n90\tThe plan-audit scans for stale/contradictory statuses each run.\n91\t\n92\t**Why mandatory, not optional:** bounded/scoped vocabulary (Option B, ratified) only\n93\tworks if a Pocket can filter \"load L1 of corespine X\" instead of opening every file\n94\tto find out what's in it. Depth/tag/status ARE the retrieval mechanism for scoped\n95\tcontext loading — without them, Option B degrades back into \"open everything.\"\n96\t\n97\t## 5. Size gate (unchanged, restated for completeness)\n98\t3,500 words / 200-line code blocks. Violation triggers §3 (mini-tree split), never\n99\t\"exceed and flag for later.\"\n100\t\n101\t## 6. Placeholder nodes (Schema Placement Engine cross-reference)\n102\tAuto-generated ancestor stubs use status `PLACEHOLDER`, depth_level `L1`, and a\n103\t`SCHEDULED` follow-up tag — see `dna/schema/CISEM-SCHEMA-00001-placement-engine.md`.\n104\t\n105\t## 7. Ratification authority — \"foundational decree\" vs \"self-ratify\" (D1)\n106\tTwo distinct acts that must never be conflated by sharing the word \"self-ratify\":\n107\t- **self-ratify (FORBIDDEN):** an AI marking its own output RATIFIED. Prohibited\n108\t  for every AI instance — \"ai_cannot: self-ratify\" (CLAUDE.md §2, ARCH-00300 Hard\n109\t  Line I7). No exceptions.\n110\t- **foundational decree (PERMITTED, Governor only):** the Governor ratifying a\n111\t  **root** governance node — one that has no upstream validator because it defines\n112\t  the validation itself (e.g. `CS-MASTER-VALIDATION-001`). A root node is ratified\n113\t  by Governor decree *without* requiring another validator to sign it. This is the\n114\t  escape from the ratification cycle (a validator that governs all corespines\n115\t  cannot itself wait for a validator).\n116\t**Rule:** foundational decree applies ONLY to nodes explicitly tagged\n117\t`root_authority: true` and is exercised ONLY by the Governor, recorded in the\n118\tnode's change log as a \"foundational decree\" with date. It is a named, bounded\n119\texception — not a general licence to skip validation. Every non-root node still\n120\tratifies through the normal validator chain once that chain exists.\n121\t\n122\t**Closed set (bounded 2026-07-16; extended 2026-07-18):** `root_authority: true` is restricted to\n123\texactly four nodes — **CISEM-FOUND-00001** (Founding), **CISEM-ARCH-00011** (this\n124\tpolicy), **CS-MASTER-VALIDATION-001** (root validator), **CISEM-ARCH-00340** (meta-protocol /\n125\tplan-creation root — added by Governor foundational decree 2026-07-18). Adding a fifth is ITSELF a\n126\tfoundational decree, logged here. Any other node carrying `root_authority` is an\n127\tinvariant violation (candidate I11). This keeps the skip-validation switch from\n128\tever spreading.\n129\t"}]},"uuid":"a27675e5-994a-4c29-b60b-be1a792b2102","timestamp":"2026-07-19T15:35:35.177Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem\\dna\\protocols\\CISEM-ARCH-00011-naming-numbering-policy.md","content":"","numLines":129,"startLine":1,"totalLines":129}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"cbd2f03a-25ea-4f84-a26b-a83a9e95aa17","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem","sessionId":"c249d411-23b2-46c5-9695-ddbaf884b7de","version":"2.1.210","gitBranch":"main","slug":"mutable-dazzling-blanket"}

Both branches proven to fire on a planted violation, both green on the real files.\n\nNow your questions — and yes, your point lands: **verifying understanding IS the crucial act.** Let me not assume you're with me; let me show my understanding and let you correct it.\n\n## PART 2 — \"Which corespine wins?\" — two concrete examples\n\nThe two roots are **CS-CREATION-001** (how things get created; doctrine D1–D6 flows down) and **CS-MASTER-VALIDATION-001** (what is valid/allowed; the global validator). They collide like this:\n\n**Example 1 — provisional use.** Creation says (via `PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE`): *\"a high-quality draft may be IN USE to make progress — bootstrap-escape.\"* Validation says: *\"nothing is binding until it passes the validator chain.\"* A `PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE` wizard just created a node. **Can that node be used?** Creation says yes (keep moving); Validation says not-yet-valid. Today we resolve it *case-by-case* with guardrails — a judgment call each time, which is the drift. Precedence settles it once: if **VALIDATION > CREATION**, no provisional use until validation signs off; if **CREATION > VALIDATION**, provisional-active is permitted and validation catches up.\n\n**Example 2 — Existing-First vs an invalid home.** Creation (§3.2b) says: *\"it EXISTS → enhance/reuse, never duplicate.\"* Validation flags that existing node as **contradictory/invalid**. **Do you build on it?** Creation says reuse (anti-duplication); Validation says that foundation is rotten, don't. If **VALIDATION > CREATION**, validation overrides Existing-First — you create fresh rather than inherit an invalid base. Without a rank, this is re-argued every time.\n\nIn both, precedence turns a recurring debate into a lookup.\n\n## PART 3 — Sealed + precedence + refusal, explained plainly + two samples\n\nThree linked pieces:\n\n1. **SEALED top-level set** — instead of *\"anyone can propose a new top-level corespine anytime\"* (OPEN), there's a **small fixed number** of top-level corespines. You don't add one casually; it takes a rare Governor **re-grounding decree**. Anything that *feels* like \"a new corespine\" is really a **branch beneath** one of the existing ones.\n2. **PRECEDENCE rank** — the top-level set is put in a **fixed order of authority**: #1 beats #2 beats #3… When two conflict, you don't debate — you look up the rank; higher wins. Deterministic.\n3. **REFUSAL-first wizard** — the wizard's **default answer is \"no, you don't need a new corespine\"**; it hands you the existing branch instead. It's built to refuse; it only permits a genuinely-new trunk via the Governor re-grounding path. The friction is the feature.\n\n**Sample A (refusal):** Someone says *\"we need a SECURITY corespine!\"* (literally our IBD-0008). The wizard checks: does \"protect the system\" already live under an existing top-level corespine (AI-behavior? operations?)? If yes → SECURITY is a **branch**, not a new trunk. Wizard **refuses** the trunk, offers the branch.\n\n**Sample B (precedence):** AI-behavior says *\"act swiftly, minimize friction.\"* Validation says *\"no action without the ratified plan.\"* They conflict on a fast move. If **VALIDATION outranks AI-BEHAVIOR**, the plan-gate wins — deterministically, every time, no re-litigation.\n\n## PART 4 — Does this respect our humble / polarity / pocket + oversight essence?\n\nThis is the real question, and my honest answer is **yes — but only if we seal the right thing.** Here's the reconciliation, and where I'd push back on a naive version:\n\n- **What gets sealed is the BOUNDARY, not the PATH (D2).** We hardcode *WHAT must stay true* — the small set of top-level domains + their precedence — and leave *HOW you work within each domain* fully open. That's D2 verbatim: \"fixed ends, free means.\" The seal is on the **trunk**; the **canopy** (branches, leaves, all the HOW) stays open and AI-explored.\n- **It IS the D6 polarity, not a break from it.** The seal is the **stable pole**; the open branches + the AI pocket reasoning within them is the **evolving pole**. Lose the seal → drift (unbounded corespine sprawl, no conflict resolution). Lose the openness → ossify. Holding both is the design. A sealed trunk with an open canopy is *literally* the polarity.\n- **The pocket + oversight survive intact (Creation Triad).** Within each domain the AI pocket still reasons freely and declares intent; oversight (RQC) audits **both** that the seal holds (no unauthorized new trunk) **and** that the branches stay healthy. All three legs remain.\n- **Sealing is the MORE humble stance, not less.** An open set lets any AI session mint a new top-level authority whenever it feels like it — that's the arrogant default. Sealing says *\"we don't get to keep inventing foundations; the foundation is small and we respect it.\"* That's the **collaborator-not-replacer** axiom made structural.\n\n**My honest caveat (pushback on the naive version):** a *wrong* seal ossifies — if we seal the wrong set or wrong order, we've hardcoded a mistake at the root. So two conditions are non-negotiable: **(a)** the seal is reached through the dwelling/consensus cycle, never rushed; **(b)** the seal is itself **re-groundable by Governor foundational decree** (firm, D1 — but not frozen; D6). Firm-but-re-groundable is the balance. With those two, it fully honors our essence. Without them, it's exactly the ossification you're right to worry about.\n\nAnd notice — **we already do this in three places:** `root_authority` is explicitly sealed at 4; the axioms are effectively sealed at A1–A8 (extended only by decree); the TYPE registry is a soft seal. So sealing isn't foreign to CISEM — it's a pattern we already trust, just never named as a reusable primitive.\n\n## PART 5 — Cross-domain extraction (parked) + \"are questions corespine material?\"\n\nI did the deep-dive and **parked it** (you asked me to register, never leave waiting) → **[IBD-0011](dna/ibd/IBD-0011-cross-domain-essence-harvest-2026-07-19.md)**. THE KEY REALIZATION — three patterns CISEM ALREADY uses LOCALLY but never GENERALIZED\nThe external inputs describe as \"new\" several things CISEM already does in ONE spot each. The value is to NAME them as reusable primitives and apply them consistently.\n- **SEALED-SET** — already live at: `root_authority` (sealed at 4, ARCH-00011 §7), Axioms (sealed at A1–A8, extend-by-decree), TYPE registry (soft seal). NOT generalized. → Candidate primitive: \"a bounded set whose membership changes only by foundational decree.\" Where else it could apply: the invariant set I1–In (currently OPEN — should it be? or is open correct because preventions only grow, D3?), the Doctrine (D1–D6, effectively sealed), the §3 gate list.\n- **PRECEDENCE / deterministic conflict-resolution by fixed rank** — already live at: the §3 HARD GATES *run in a fixed order* (3.0→3.1→3.2a→3.2b→…); ARCH-00011 \"on conflict, ARCH-00011 wins\"; VOC mirrors \"on conflict, ARCH-00011 wins.\" NOT generalized. → Candidate primitive: a global PRECEDENCE table for ALL governance conflicts (corespine vs corespine, invariant vs invariant — does I19 beat I23?, axiom vs axiom, gate vs gate). This is B1 (the big gift) generalized beyond corespines.\n- **PLANTED-VIOLATION PROOF (activation-proof)** — just done for the [RAW-PAIR] check (2026-07-19). NOT mandatory. → Candidate primitive: EVERY mechanical check ships with a planted-violation test proving it fires (DONE = wired+called+verified, A6). Home: the check-authoring convention + RQC audit.\n\n## 2. WHERE EACH WIZARD ESSENCE APPLIES BEYOND CORESPINES\n- **A1 uniqueness/refuse-first gate** → ALL creation, not just corespines: nodes, skills, agents, vocabulary terms, plans. \"Refuse-first\" as the default posture of EVERY creation wizard (cisem-create/meta/plan). Existing-First (§3.2b) is the seed; make it a hard pre-wizard gate everywhere.\n- **A2 \"what BREAKS if absent?\" root-goal test** → every node's Goal-First (§3.1), every plan's goal, every skill's reason-to-exist. A sharper, falsifiable goal test platform-wide.\n- **A3 TELL vs RULE (≥1 must be mechanical)** → every invariant (is each I mechanically checked or just documented? — audit I1–In for TELL-only ones), every gate, every \"enforcement\" claim. Candidate: a mandatory `enforcement_type: TELL|RULE` field on every governance element; ≥1 RULE or it's \"just a doc.\" This IS EXISTS≠ACTIVE (I23) as a typed field.\n- **A4 Cannot-Mean / explicit exclusions mandatory** → every node (penumbra/silent_on), every vocabulary term (what it does NOT mean), every axiom (its boundary). Candidate: a universal mandatory `cannot_mean:` field in ARCH-00230 creation checklist.\n- **A5 born-DECLARED honest wiring** → already universal (4 wiring states). Reinforce: nothing is born LIVE.\n- **A6 proof-not-optimism exit** → every gate + check (see planted-violation primitive above). Every done-claim cites disk-verifiable evidence (I22).\n- **B2 refusal-as-product** → generalize: a creation wizard's PRIMARY value is what it REFUSES, not what it emits. Reframes ALL wizards.\n- **B3 classifier-first default-no** → every creation entry point defaults to \"you probably don't need a new X; here's the existing home.\"\n- **B5 FLEXIBLE vs NOT-FLEXIBLE tagging** → every decision in every node tagged config-adjustable vs constitutional. Validate against our waivable/governed/absolute 3-tier (2-tier vs 3-tier reconciliation).\n\n## 3. \"ARE 'QUESTIONS AS CONTEXT / DNA CARRIERS' CORESPINE MATERIAL?\" — analysis\n**Short answer: NOT on its own — but it may be a BRANCH under a candidate EPISTEMOLOGY corespine.**\n- \"Questions carry context\" (IBD-0009 #2) is a property of the REPRESENTATION FORMAT — every principle ships with its validation questions so it inherits WITH its meaning. That is cross-cutting representational rule, not a governance DOMAIN. → best placed as: (a) an A6 enhancement + (b) a MANDATORY field in the creation checklist (every principle/node carries its validation questions). By the sharper root-goal test (A2): \"what breaks if it's absent?\" = \"principles inherit bare and get freestyled\" — real, but that's an anti-drift FIELD, not a whole domain. So: axiom + format material, not a trunk.\n- **BUT — the bigger candidate (worth a real look):** cluster \"questions-carry-context\" + \"concept↔essence polarity\" + \"the creation/dwelling cycle\" + **\"verification of understanding is crucial\"** (Governor's meta-point this session) + \"examples carry context like questions.\" Together these describe HOW CISEM ESTABLISHES, VERIFIES, AND TRANSMITS UNDERSTANDING. That is a coherent DOMAIN — an **EPISTEMOLOGY / KNOWLEDGE-REPRESENTATION corespine** (candidate). Its primary concern: \"how does CISEM know what it knows, verify understanding before acting, and carry meaning across inheritance?\" If it passes the \"what breaks if absent?\" test (≈ \"meaning drifts, understanding is assumed not verified, principles inherit hollow\") it may be trunk-level — OR a major branch under CS-CREATION-001. Questions-as-carriers would then be ONE branch of it, not the whole thing.\n- **Decision to bring to consensus:** does an EPISTEMOLOGY domain earn a top-level slot (relevant to the SEALED-set question — what ARE the top-level corespines?), or is it a branch under Creation? Do NOT decide alone. Flag for the top-level-set discussion.\n\n## 4. ISSUES TO EXPLORE (parked, each needs its own threshold pass)\n- Should the invariant set I1–In be SEALED or stay OPEN? (D3 says preventions only grow → maybe OPEN is correct; but no precedence among invariants = latent I-vs-I conflict.)\n- Build the global PRECEDENCE table (generalize B1): rank corespines AND resolve invariant-vs-invariant, gate-vs-gate. Any concept can, in principle, become a new trunk, and when two corespines give conflicting instructions there is no deterministic winner — each clash is re-argued.\n\n**Cause:** an *open, unranked* forest has neither **membership discipline** (→ trunk sprawl; A2 \"everything is part of a corespine\" loses meaning if trunks multiply freely) nor **conflict resolution** (→ the Q8 drift, re-litigated every time).\n\n**Resolution — the decision:**\n\n| | **SEALED + precedence-ranked** (recommended) | **OPEN forest** |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Pros** | Deterministic conflict resolution (Q8 solved permanently); membership discipline; enables refusal-first wizard; consistent with root_authority@4 / axioms@8; tree becomes legible (every corespine has a known trunk + rank) | Maximum flexibility; never blocked from adding a domain; no risk of a wrong seal |\n| **Cons** | A *wrong* seal ossifies (hardcodes a root mistake); requires naming the set + order now (careful dwelling, upfront cost) | Q8 stays unresolved forever; trunk sprawl; wizard can't be refusal-first; contradicts our own existing sealed sets |\n\n**Recommendation (one):** **SEAL the top-level set + assign a precedence rank + make the seal re-groundable by Governor foundational decree.** This is the D6 polarity done right — the *trunk* is firm (D1, recurring), the *canopy* (branches + all the HOW) stays open (D2, seal the boundary not the path), and the re-grounding escape hatch prevents ossification (firm, not frozen). Now N+1. Next week: CS-LOGGING-001, CS-BACKUP-001… **sprawl.** And is \"security\" really a *peer* of Creation and Validation? Unclear, and nobody's forced to ask.\n- **SEALED world:** the refusal-first wizard asks *\"does 'protect the system' already live under an existing top-level domain?\"* Security's essence — refusing malicious input, integrity, trust — is **how the AI behaves safely** → a **branch under AI-BEHAVIOR** (or Operations), not a new trunk. Good catch.\n\nBut now let me be the expert you asked for and **push back on the opposite over-correction**, because \"AI decides each conflict and the DNA evolves by itself\" has three real failure modes, and naming them is how we make your vision *safe*:\n\n1. **No default floor → drift and non-determinism.** If *every* conflict is a fresh AI deliberation, the *same* conflict can resolve differently across two sessions. That is precisely the AI instability you said we're here to avoid. A system with no presumption isn't flexible — it's unpredictable.\n2. **Self-enactment → unbounded drift.** \"DNA evolves by itself\" is healthy only if it means the system *proposes* its own evolution and a gate *ratifies* it. Self-evolution that also self-enacts is the runaway case (D5 + A4 forbid it). The line between \"self-improving\" and \"unstable\" is exactly *propose-then-ratify*.\n3. **Deliberation cost.** If a trivial conflict escalates to the PE engine every time, the common case gets slow and noisy.\n\nSo the balanced resolution is **not open-vs-rigid — it's three layers**, and it dissolves the false choice:\n\n- **Layer 1 — a DEFAULT presumption (the floor).** For the common case, a conflict resolves *instantly and deterministically* by a ratified default. This is the guardrail against drift. **But \"sealed\" here means \"the current ratified presumption,\" not \"frozen.\"**\n- **Layer 2 — DEFEASANCE by risk-tiered oversight.** When the PE engine judges the default a poor fit for *this* context, it can override it — but through your protocol: **assess risk → if LOW, resolve provisionally and proceed immediately (progress) + park for ratification (respect); if HIGH, block and escalate to the Governor before acting.** The decision is *never final until ratified.* This is your exact vision — I'm just anchoring it to a floor so it can't drift.\n- **Layer 3 — the LEARNING LOOP (the part that's genuinely yours and genuinely better).** Every conflict + its provisional resolution + its eventual ratification becomes **data**. When a conflict recurs and resolves the same way, the RQC *proposes* codifying it — **narrowing** where we found a gap, or **expanding** a rule (your own example: \"no creation without a plan\" → \"…unless it clears the SWIFT gates\"). The DNA evolves *from lived conflict*, not from armchair design — but it evolves by **proposing**, and the Governor (or a defined risk-tiered protocol) **ratifies**.\n\nUnder this, **\"sealed\" = \"the presumption that holds until argument-weight, through the protocol, reopens it.\"** That is your axiom, made into an engine.\n\n## Your axiom — adopt it, with one guardrail, and note it already reconciles with D3\n\n> *\"Nothing is a constant axiom. All can be challenged, provided the weight of arguments justifies reopening a sealed element.\"*\n\n**I recommend adopting it** — it's the meta-principle that makes \"sealed ≠ frozen\" coherent, and it's more honest than pretending anything is eternal. Two things to make it safe rather than corrosive:\n\n- **Challengeable ≠ free.** Reopening costs *argument-weight* and runs *through the predefined protocol* to *Governor ratification*. Otherwise \"everything is always up for grabs\" becomes its own instability. The bar is the guardrail.\n- **It already fits D3.** D3 says preventions are permanent + cumulative, and *removing one needs a foundational decree.* That \"foundational decree\" **is** your argument-weight gate. It's a *composition* of what we already have — PE pocket (ARCH-00240) + RQC (ARCH-00320) as the oversight; PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE + PARK-BY-DEMAND + the queue as \"provisional, not final\"; the threshold + SWIFT as the risk assessment; the learning-registry as the loop; Governor decree as ratification. The one genuinely-missing piece is the **ledger** — which is exactly the gap you sensed.\n\n---\n\nTwo things I'd want from you before we go further (and I'm deliberately *not* building any of this yet):\n\n1. {"parentUuid":"69959c75-4c1f-43ee-9deb-6ac24dc0a5b2","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdBjVvWJ1NKVtYC2Fv3G8","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01CuSW4Jbxf7Fj9qLm6srprh","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem\\dna\\ibd\\IBD-0012-conflict-model-and-axioms-2026-07-19.md","content":"# IBD-0012 — Conflict-Resolution Model (APPROVED) + Axiom Candidates + Top-Level-Significance (2026-07-19)\n**Type:** IBD (vault park) | **Status:** MIXED — the conflict MODEL is Governor-APPROVED (2026-07-19) as the direction, NOT yet a ratified plan; the axiom candidates + the top-level question are PARKED-RAW (run the 8-Q stress-test before ratifying).\n**Why this exists:** Governor approved parking this (\"2 you can place it in IBD\"). Register everything; never leave it in chat.\n**Feeds:** the top-level-corespine-set decision + the future conflict-protocol plan + the axiom set (FOUND-00001 / A-series).\n\n## 1. THE CONFLICT-RESOLUTION MODEL — Governor-APPROVED direction (2026-07-19; \"1 three approved\")\nNot open-vs-rigid (open forest RULED-OUT-PERMANENT, DEC-0001). The design is a **SCALE**, not a static winner:\n\n**Layer 1 — DEFAULT presumption (the floor).** Common-case conflicts resolve INSTANTLY + DETERMINISTICALLY by a\nratified default precedence. This is the guardrail against AI non-determinism/drift. \"Sealed\" here = \"the current\nratified presumption,\" NOT \"frozen.\" Without a floor, every conflict is a fresh deliberation = the drift we fight.\n\n**Layer 2 — a SCALE that triages each conflict (Governor clarification 2026-07-19 — NOT \"AI deliberates every conflict\"):**\nthe scale decides WHEN the rigid default fires vs WHEN a conflict is vaulted. Bands:\n  - **RIGID-DEFAULT fires** — trivial/known conflict → the ratified precedence applies, no deliberation.\n  - **PROVISIONAL-PROCEED + PARK** — low-risk, resolvable now → AI resolves provisionally, proceeds immediately\n    (progress), and PARKS the decision for ratification (respect). Never final until ratified.\n  - **VAULT-AND-HALT** — hard/fundamental clash → the platform STOPS and says, humbly, *\"we have an internal\n    conflict; something fundamental is clashing — we'll get back to you.\"* Vaulted for reconciliation (→ archive\n    VAULTED-CONFLICT, e.g. DEC-0004). **Applies to BOTH internal development AND external apps/solutions built on\n    CISEM** — a deployed solution hitting an internal governance conflict degrades gracefully (\"internal conflict,\n    we'll get back to you\") instead of forcing a wrong answer. Risk-tiered: high-risk/hard → halt; never proceed provisionally.\n\n**Layer 3 — the LEARNING LOOP (evolve the DNA from lived conflict).** Every conflict + its resolution + its\nratification is DATA. Recurring conflicts → the RQC PROPOSES codifying: NARROW where a gap was found, or EXPAND a\nrule (Governor's own example: \"no governed creation without a ratified plan\" → \"…unless it clears the SWIFT gates\").\n**Propose-then-ratify, NEVER self-enact** (D5 + A4) — self-evolution that self-ratifies is the runaway case.\n\n**Existing-First:** almost all of this is COMPOSITION of existing machinery — PE pocket (ARCH-00240) + RQC (ARCH-00320)\n= oversight; PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE + PARK-BY-DEMAND + queue = \"provisional, not final\"; threshold (CS-THRESHOLD-001) +\nSWIFT = risk assessment; learning-registry = the loop; Governor decree = ratification. The one genuinely-new piece\nwas the durable ledger — now built (dna/archive/archive-ledger.yaml, executes BP-0008).\n\n**Opus expert caveats (kept on record):** (a) the DEFAULT floor is non-negotiable — a pure \"AI decides each conflict\"\nreintroduces AI's own instability; (b) self-evolution must PROPOSE, never enact; (c) the VAULT-AND-HALT band must be\nreserved for genuinely-hard conflicts or everything stalls. These are the guardrails that make the vision safe.\n\n## 2. AXIOM CANDIDATES (PARKED — need the 8-Q stress-test; Opus CANNOT ratify)\n- **AX-CAND-A \"Constant = temporarily valid\" (Governor, revised 2026-07-19):** *\"The world has constant dynamics;\n  everything changes. We hold complementary polarities defining supporting elements to the Essence. So all things\n  defined as constant have only TEMPORARY validity — until a better version is presented AND VERIFIED.\"* Opus read:\n  strong; the \"and verified\" ties it to I22 (no unverified done) — the mature form of D6 + challengeability. GUARDRAIL\n  needed or it corrodes: reopening a sealed element costs ARGUMENT-WEIGHT + runs the predefined protocol + Governor\n  ratification (challengeable ≠ free). RECONCILES with D3 (preventions cumulative; removal needs a foundational decree)\n  — that decree IS the argument-weight gate. The axiom is recursively self-applying (it, too, is challengeable).\n- **AX-CAND-B \"Nothing is a constant axiom / all challengeable with sufficient weight\"** — earlier form of AX-CAND-A;\n  fold together. One axiom, not two.\n\n## 3. TOP-LEVEL-CORESPINE SIGNIFICANCE — the \"slippery\" question (Governor 2026-07-19)\n\"Top-level = the one with the most significant tree under it. What is significant — the NUMBER of elements, or the\nSIGNIFICANCE in the system?\" Governor's method: BUILD several corespines we think are significant; looking at them\nreveals the answer (resolve-by-doing). **Opus expert read:** significance = **GOVERNING REACH**, not element count.\nA top-level corespine is one whose constraints bind the WIDEST set of descendants (transitive inheritance) + whose\nremoval breaks ≈everything in its domain (\"what breaks if absent?\") + which is NOT itself a branch of another domain's\nconcern. Element-count is a WEAK proxy (a big shallow pile ≠ significant; a small deep root can be).
