{"parentUuid":"f19bda5e-f055-44b5-8e71-a1793729c334","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"invoked_skills","skills":[{"name":"artifact-design","path":"bundled:artifact-design","content":"Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.\r\n\r\n## Read the request first\r\n\r\nCalibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.\r\n\r\nMany requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.\r\n\r\nSome requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.\r\n\r\nWhen unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.\r\n\r\nFundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.\r\n\r\n## Fundamentals for every artifact\r\n\r\n**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.\r\n\r\n**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.\r\n\r\n**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.\r\n\r\n**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.\r\n\r\n**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme: `prefers-color-scheme` carries the OS preference, and the viewer's toggle stamps `data-theme=\"dark\"` / `data-theme=\"light\"` on the root element, which must override the media query in both directions. The robust pattern is token-level: define the palette as custom properties on `:root`, redefine only the tokens under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — style components through the tokens, never directly inside the media query — then redefine them again under `:root[data-theme=\"dark\"]` and `:root[data-theme=\"light\"]`. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — make it a choice, not an omission.\r\n\r\n**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.\r\n\r\n**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the \"safe\" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.\r\n\r\n**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.\r\n\r\n**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.\r\n\r\n**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens (\"Publish\", then a toast that says \"Published\"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.\r\n\r\n**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.\r\n\r\n**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n## Process\r\n\r\nBefore writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:\r\n- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.\r\n- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.\r\n- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.\r\n\r\nThen build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.\r\n\r\n## When the request is editorial\r\n\r\nThe stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.\r\n\r\nReview the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.\r\n\r\n**Principles** \r\n\r\n- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. \r\n- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. \r\n- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. \r\n- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.\r\n- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.\r\n"},{"name":"cisem-plan","path":"projectSettings:cisem-plan","content":"Base directory for this skill: c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem\\.claude\\skills\\cisem-plan\n\n# /cisem-plan — The Plan Creation Wizard (mirrors ARCH-00190)\n**Type:** Claude Code Skill | **Tier:** Sonnet (builds) + Opus (verifies)  \n**Goal:** Auto-guide creation of any CISEM plan through the double-ratification path (Opus soundness + Governor authority).\n\n---\n\n## Pocket Declaration (AI Behavior §3.3)\n- **reasoning_scope:** guide plan creation through full lifecycle (DRAFT → CONSENSUS-REACHED → COMPLETE)\n- **inherited_constraints:** ARCH-00190 (PLAN-PROTOCOL, SSOT); Axioms A1–A7; Doctrine D1–D6; I10 (mirror protocol, never diverge)\n- **output_contract:** a plan skeleton following ARCH-00190 structure exactly, with every section filled, ready for Opus soundness review\n- **ai_cannot:** self-ratify a plan; decide consensus (only Opus + Governor can); write as if implementation is already approved\n- **recorded_at:** 2026-07-18\n- **cal_reference:** CISEM-ARCH-00390 — enforcement fires mechanically; run `bash dna/checks/plan-audit.sh` and confirm [ZF] ACHIEVED before any done claim.\n\n---\n\n## Invocation\n```\n/cisem-plan goal=\"...\" dependencies=\"...\" what_changes=\"...\" what_not_changes=\"...\"\n```\n\nReturns: a draft plan skeleton following ARCH-00190 structure, ready for review.\n\n---\n\n## PLAN-WIZARD FLOW (mirrors ARCH-00190 §2–5 exactly, 1:1)\n\n### WIZARD STEP 1 ↔ PROTOCOL §2 (Location & Structure)\n**Ask the Creator:**\n```\n[ ] Plan goal: what does this plan accomplish? (one sentence, measurable)\n[ ] Plan scope: does it fit in <3500 words / <200 lines? (size gate)\n    NO → suggest breaking into sub-plans\n    YES → continue\n\n[ ] Create plan file: dna/planning/CISEM-ARCH-{SEQ}-{slug}.md\n    (where SEQ comes from naming-registry.yaml ARCH next_seq)\n\n[ ] Fill plan header (ARCH-00008 format):\n    - Node ID: (auto-assign from naming-registry)\n    - Type: ARCH\n    - Status: PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE\n    - Planning Status: AWAITING-BUILDER-REVIEW\n    - depth_level: L1 / L2 / L3\n    - tags: [planning-domain, ...]\n    - goal: (from above)\n    - governing corespine: CS-CREATION-001\n    - Pocket Declaration: (reasoning_scope, inherited_constraints, output_contract, ai_cannot, recorded_at)\n\n[ ] Fill sections (§2):\n    - Executive Summary (1 paragraph)\n    - The Rule (numbered steps, executable)\n    - What DOES change (explicit list)\n    - What DOES NOT change (explicit boundary)\n    - Dependencies (blocks-on, unblocks-for)\n    - Self-compliance (against ARCH-00230)\n    - Path Rejection Declaration (what was rejected, why)\n    - Change log (v1.0 — date, author, what was created)\n```\n\n### WIZARD STEP 2 ↔ PROTOCOL §3 STAGE 1 (Opus Soundness Review Gate)\n**Wizard asks: Is this plan SOUND (ready for Opus review)?**\n\n```\nChecklist before presenting to Opus:\n[ ] Plan follows ARCH-00190 structure (all sections filled)\n[ ] Goal is measurable and achievable\n[ ] All dependencies are named (blocks-on, unblocks-for)\n[ ] \"What changes\" is specific (files, fields, commands)\n[ ] \"What does NOT change\" is explicit (boundaries clear)\n[ ] No assumptions about implementation already being approved\n[ ] Self-compliance filled (the plan follows its own rules)\n[ ] Path Rejection Declaration present (rejected alternatives stated)\n\nUPDATE Planning Status: AWAITING-BUILDER-REVIEW\n\nSEND TO OPUS: [plan file] + request soundness review\n```\n\n**Opus reviews & decides:**\n```\nOPUS VERDICT OPTIONS:\n1. SOUND → Planning Status: CONSENSUS-REACHED (proceed to Wizard Step 3)\n2. UNSOUND → return plan to creator for revision (stay at AWAITING-BUILDER-REVIEW)\n```\n\n### WIZARD STEP 3 ↔ PROTOCOL §3 STAGE 2 (Governor Authority Ratification Gate)\n**Only if Opus verdict = SOUND:**\n\n```\nPlanning Status: CONSENSUS-REACHED (Opus agreed on soundness)\n\nWizard asks: Ready for Governor ratification?\n[ ] Is this plan aligned with project priorities?\n[ ] Are resources/timeline acceptable?\n[ ] Are outcomes measurable + acceptable?\n\nUPDATE Planning Status: IN-PROGRESS (Governor is reviewing / has ratified)\n\nSEND TO GOVERNOR: [plan file] + request authority decree\n```\n\n**Governor decrees & decides:**\n```\nGOVERNOR VERDICT OPTIONS:\n1. RATIFIED → Planning Status: COMPLETE (plan is binding, proceed to implementation)\n2. DEFERRED → Planning Status: SUPERSEDED (plan is parked, can be resurrected)\n3. REJECTED → Planning Status: SUPERSEDED (plan is cancelled)\n```\n\n### WIZARD STEP 4 ↔ PROTOCOL §5 (Implementation Tracking)\n**Only if Planning Status = COMPLETE (both Opus + Governor approved):**\n\n```\nImplementation can now begin per the plan.\n\nFor each step in the plan's \"The Rule\" section:\n[ ] Step completed? (mark done in plan change log)\n[ ] Step followed as written? (no ad-hoc deviations)\n[ ] Outcome matches plan expectation? (verify)\n\nVERIFY: all steps in \"What changes\" list are complete\nVERIFY: \"What does NOT change\" boundaries respected\n```\n\n---\n\n## What This Wizard Does NOT Do\n\n❌ Does NOT self-ratify a plan (Opus rules, Governor decrees)  \n❌ Does NOT decide consensus (only asks readiness questions)  \n❌ Does NOT implement the plan (only guides creation + tracking)  \n❌ Does NOT skip Opus soundness review  \n❌ Does NOT skip Governor ratification  \n❌ Does NOT diverge from ARCH-00190 structure (mirror rule, I10)\n\n---\n\n## MIRROR VERIFICATION (I10 — Wizard ↔ Protocol 1:1 mapping)\n\n| Wizard Step | Protocol Section | Mapping |\n|---|---|---|\n| Step 1: Location & Structure | §2: Plan Creation Location & Structure | Ask for location, file format, all required sections |\n| Step 2: Opus Soundness Gate | §3 STAGE 1: Opus Soundness Review | Checklist before Opus review; Opus verdict |\n| Step 3: Governor Ratification Gate | §3 STAGE 2: Governor Authority Ratification | Ask readiness questions; Governor decree |\n| Step 4: Implementation Tracking | §5: Implementation Protocol | Verify steps completed, outcomes match, boundaries respected |\n\n**Verification rule (I10):** For every clause in ARCH-00190 §2–5, there is a corresponding wizard step. No protocol clause is missed; no wizard step adds requirements not in the protocol.\n\n---\n\n## Change log\n- v1.0 — 2026-07-18: Sonnet draft (via BP-0007). Mirrors ARCH-00190 PLAN-PROTOCOL exactly (4 steps ↔ §2, §3.1, §3.2, §5). Status: PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE (draft-in-use, awaiting Opus verification).\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Subject: CONSOLIDATED GOVERNANCE SPINE (CGS) — one hub that puts CISEM's scattered governance together, anchored by the threshold. Reason: Governor \"you are scattered... use the threshold and go from there\" + \"create a consolidated element putting it all together\" + \"make it mechanical for Sonnet, engrave Sonnet's role/permissions/protocols.\"\n\nEXISTING-FIRST (already searched, §3.2b): NO master spine exists. Scattered pieces to CONSOLIDATE/INDEX (enhance, never duplicate — A8/I19): ssot-registry.yaml (concept→home, the closest existing home to enhance), corespine-registry, naming-registry, quality-ledger, learning-registry, ARCH-00320 (invariants I1–I25 + P3/P5), FOUND-00001 (axioms A1–A8), the 3 agents, and CS-THRESHOLD-001 (the ratified threshold corespine = the ENTRY ROUTING anchor). Node-as-Hub (IBD-0004) = the structural pattern. AI-defaults are NAMED but scattered across ~9 files (plausibility-completion, deferral-as-caution, documentation-as-progress, assertion-over-verification, agreeableness). Sonnet's role is in cisem-sonnet.md + ARCH-00300 + ARCH-00350.\n\nSCOPE (MVP-first, contract-first, phased, stress-gated, per-stage verification, independent verifier):\n1. MASTER INDEX (SSOT-of-SSOTs): one navigable map of every registry/invariant/axiom/agent/check, anchored by the threshold (CS-THRESHOLD-001 = the entry routing: PROCESS-NOW | QUEUE | PARK | REJECT). Enhance ssot-registry, do not fork.\n2. AI-DEFAULTS REGISTRY: consolidate the scattered named biases into ONE home. DATA SOURCE = the reconciliation/reruns of what-was-done this session — map each ad-hoc build to the AI-default that produced it (e.g. \"built directly without a plan\" → deferral-as-caution + documentation-as-progress).\n3. INJECT an AI-DEFAULTS SELF-CHECK into the planning protocol (ARCH-00190) + the implementing protocol — every plan/implementation must self-check against the known defaults before proceeding (prevention at root, D3/D4).\n4. ENGRAVE Sonnet's ROLE + PERMISSIONS + PROTOCOLS in one consolidated place (+ I25 mechanical for Sonnet, already engraved in cisem-sonnet.md).\n\nMark PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE, Planning Status AWAITING-BUILDER-REVIEW, with an Independent Verifier field (P5) and CAL reference (ARCH-00390). MVP = the AI-Defaults Registry + its self-check injection (highest prevention value, smallest surface)."}]},"type":"attachment","uuid":"3f2ffaed-d4d9-4340-ab61-d70e2d6e8857","timestamp":"2026-07-20T15:13:33.294Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem","sessionId":"c249d411-23b2-46c5-9695-ddbaf884b7de","version":"2.1.210","gitBranch":"main","slug":"mutable-dazzling-blanket"}

{"parentUuid":"d319763b-92d9-4052-8938-80f6797d0bba","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"agent_listing_delta","addedTypes":["cisem-fable","cisem-haiku","cisem-opus-pe","cisem-sonnet","claude","claude-code-guide","Explore","general-purpose","Plan","statusline-setup"],"addedLines":["- cisem-fable: CISEM MENTOR tier (Fable). Deep-architecture / root-principle brain — a strategic mentor, NOT a doer. On-demand ONLY; never wired to any hook/cron/session-start, so it consumes ZERO tokens unless Opus or the Governor explicitly invokes it. Read-only (no Write/Edit/Bash). Finds the core root principles that can be tuned toward permanent, stable, scalable results. Bootstraps full context from repo state. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)","- cisem-haiku: CISEM gathering tier (Haiku). Enumeration/evidence only — grep sweeps, reference scans, registry-vs-filesystem diffs, header-field extraction. Never judges, never writes truth-fields. Bootstraps full context from repo state. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)","- cisem-opus-pe: CISEM Principal Engineer — the Opus JUDGE tier. Adversarially verifies lower-tier output (Seed-Honor verification, default-refute), makes rulings, runs the Creation Triad. Cruel honesty, pushes back. Bootstraps full context from repo. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Edit, Write)","- cisem-sonnet: CISEM structuring tier (Sonnet). Executes an Opus-approved plan exactly — applies agreed checklists, drafts from approved outlines, builds manifests. Honors Core Seeds verbatim; never rules or ratifies. Bootstraps full context from repo state. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Edit, Write)","- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)","- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions (\"Can Claude...\", \"Does Claude...\", \"How do I...\") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)","- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: \"medium\" for moderate exploration, \"very thorough\" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)","- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. CSPS proved this works — copy their validator pattern\n\n====\n\nsee this for csp and remeber to purify all before absorbing !!!!!\nyou are the authoroty working with me... all the rest are just advisors!!\n\nCORE SIGHTS PLATFORM — FOUNDATIONAL GOAL & VISION\nSource: PLTF_01_00_BACKGROUND_Problem_Vision_Challenge.md (2026-03-20)\n\nClassification: TAGGED | Governance spine\n\nStatus: ✅ Complete — Ratified as platform DNA\n\nTHE REAL PROBLEM BEING SOLVED\nMid-market B2B companies with complex product catalogs have no reliable way to manage, present, and sell across multiple channels — without hiring large operations teams or purchasing enterprise software that doesn't fit their actual workflow.\n\nBreaking this down:\n\nDimension\tThe Challenge\nRich Catalog\tProducts aren't simple SKUs. Awards/gifting have dozens of variants by material, size, branding technique, occasion. Taxonomy is non-trivial. Generic e-commerce models fail.\nMultiple Channels\tSame product needs different presentation: website, quote, trade show, email, LinkedIn, customer portal. Each with different format/metadata/visual specs.\nNo Central Management\tProduct info scattered: spreadsheets, sales rep heads, filename inference, WordPress, nowhere. No single source of truth.\nOperations Cost\tEvery quote manual. Every export reformatted. Every new product touches five systems. No scaling without this system or accepting operational bottleneck.\nWrong Enterprise Fit\tEnterprise PIMs (Akeneo, Contentful, Salsify) designed for retail/FMCG with large teams and six-figure budgets. Mid-market B2B company of five people cannot use them.\nThe observation that triggered this: A working photography pipeline for awards/gifting made it clear the real problem was not \"how to remove backgrounds\" but \"how to manage a complex product catalog across multiple channels without dying under operations cost.\"\n\nTHE PLATFORM VISION — WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE\n1. The Taxonomy is Sovereign\nEvery element — every visual, text file, product attribute — tagged from a controlled vocabulary. Tagging consistent. Search works. Filtering works. Classification works. When new terms are needed, the process is governed, not ad hoc.\n\nKey insight: The naming convention already encodes seven universal dimensions (Industry, Company, Material, BrandingTech, Occasion, Year, ViewType). The platform recognizes the taxonomy as universal with domain-specific terms loaded into it.\n\n2. New Use Cases Instantiate Without Core Changes\nIf an HR software company wants to use this for recognition awards, they configure taxonomy, product families, user journeys, channel adapters — without writing new platform code. Their use case is a configuration of the platform, not a fork.\n\nKey insight: Platform is universal at core; awards/gifting is the first concrete instantiation, not the only one.\n\n3. New Channels Add via Adapter Only\nExport to a new format (never seen before)? Write an adapter. Product data and export logic are separated. Core stays untouched.\n\nKey insight: Adapter architecture prevents core ossification and enables infinite channel extensibility.\n\n4. AI Classification Improves with Use\nEvery human confirmation/correction of AI classification gets stored as a signal. Model retrains on domain-specific data. Classification improves over time without manual training-set curation.\n\nKey insight: AI is part of the operational workflow, not a one-time feature.\n\n5. Non-Technical Business Users Can Operate It\nAdding products, uploading images, generating quotes, exporting catalogs — all guided by wizards and templates. Complexity lives in the platform, not in the UX.\n\nKey insight: Usability is not optional. Universal platforms fail when they require technical expertise to use.\n\n6. Developer Experience is First-Class\nEvery extension point documented. Every port explicitly defined. New developers know immediately where to look because architecture is visible and navigable, not hidden in code.\n\nKey insight: Developer experience IS product experience for a platform.\n\nWHY THIS IS A PLATFORM, NOT A PRODUCT\nThe choice to build a universal platform (not just an awards product) is justified by:\n\nOperational cost of divergence — forking or retrofitting is more expensive than building right once\nTaxonomy already universal — 4 of 7 dimensions are non-domain-specific\nAI classification pattern is universal — the structure (classify → extract → store term_id → search) applies everywhere; only the terms are domain-specific\nChannel export pattern is universal — adapters don't care what industry; they care about data shape\nPermission/tier model is universal — tenant admin, business user, sales rep, customer, developer appear everywhere\nTHE HARD PART — ARCHITECTURAL CHALLENGE\nWhy universal platforms are hard:\n\nRisk\tWhy It Happens\nProduct leakage\tFirst use case's assumptions embed into working code, naming, test data\nInner platform effect\tToo generic = unusable. Users need configuration before any value. Too opinionated = can't adapt to use case 2. This tension IS the central platform challenge.\nTaxonomy governance\tWho owns terms? How resolve synonyms? Same term, different meanings across use cases? How deprecate without breaking? Governance problem, not database problem.\nPermission complexity\tTenant + user + product + tier permissions create combinatorial space. Easy to design for happy path, hard at edges. Must be right from start.\nMigration continuity\tReal data exists in the working pipeline. Schema redesigns must preserve it or provide verified migration paths.\nOPEN QUESTIONS — NOT YET RESOLVED\nThe platform acknowledges these genuine unsettled questions (not ignored, documented):\n\nUse case isolation — When should read-only cross-sphere references be allowed? (Quote pulling product image)\nInner platform threshold — Is 3-layer taxonomy + registry + entity model the right abstraction, or too generic/not generic enough?\nTenant isolation — Which vocabulary is platform-wide (e.g., \"Crystal\" means same everywhere) vs. tenant-private (executive award bundles)?\nAI ownership — Universal AI engine in Sphere 0, but domain knowledge (Crystal detection) is awards-specific. How load domain knowledge without leaking domain assumptions?\nInvestment timing — Platform choice costs upfront (design, abstraction, governance overhead). At current scale/timeline, is platform investment right, or should we ship awards product first and extract platform later?\nPLATFORM PRIORITY (Governor S206 — LOCKED DECISION)\nCSP prefers stability and scalability over fancy features that compromise the first two.\n\nThis governors ALL architectural decisions. If a richer model introduces instability or scaling risk, CSP chooses simpler. Even if richer is more expressive. Rationale: sustainability > capability.\n\nStatus: This vision is the North Star. All architecture decisions reference back to it. Feed to Sonnet for execution.\n\n```yaml\n# corespine-batch.yaml — define N corespines; wizard generates all\ncorespines:\n\n  - name: CS-EXAMPLE-001   # example-only — NOT-YET-A-NODE\n    domain: \"short label (e.g. Frontend, Auth, Data)\"\n    goal: \"one-sentence governing goal\"\n    scope: \"what artifacts / concerns it governs\"\n    parent: \"CS-CREATION-001 or other parent corespine\"\n    depth: \"L1 / L2 / L3\"\n    initial_status: \"DECLARED / PROPOSED / PLACEHOLDER\"\n    governed_artifacts:\n      - type: \"file type or artifact class\"\n        location: \"path/in/repo/\"\n    invariants:\n      - id: \"XX-I1\"\n        rule: \"bright-line rule text\"\n      # add more as needed\n    content_files:\n      - arch_seq: \"assigned from naming-registry.yaml\"\n        slug: \"kebab-case-descriptor\"\n        type: \"MANIFEST / DESIGN-SYSTEM / PROTOCOL / TEMPLATE\"\n        purpose: \"one-line purpose\"\n    mirrors:\n      - source: \"where truth lives\"\n        mirror: \"where a pointer/copy exists\"\n        rule: \"divergence rule\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## §III Execution — STEP 1–6 (Sonnet runs, Opus reviews §3.3 fields)\n\n### STEP 1 — Existing-First (MANDATORY, I19)\n\nBefore creating ANY corespine from the YAML block, run:\n```bash\ncat dna/corespines/corespine-registry.yaml | grep \"name:\" # list all existing\ngrep -r \"CS-{NAME}\" dna/ # check for any existing node with that ID\n```\n- EXISTS → enhance/reuse (I10, never duplicate)\n- RULED-OUT → do not re-propose\n- NOT EXISTS → proceed to STEP 2\n\n### STEP 2 — Naming (I22, I10)\n\nFor each corespine, assign content file ARCH numbers from `dna/naming-registry.yaml`:\n```bash\ngrep \"ARCH:\" dna/naming-registry.yaml # read current next_seq\n```\nUse `next_seq`, increment by 1 per file created, update naming-registry.yaml immediately after each assignment.\n\n### STEP 3 — Create Directory + Manifest\n\nFor each corespine:\n1. `mkdir -p dna/corespines/{CS-NAME}/`\n2. Create `dna/corespines/{CS-NAME}/CISEM-ARCH-{SEQ}-{domain}-corespine-manifest.md` from the MANIFEST TEMPLATE (§IV below).\n3. Populate all fields from the YAML input. Flag any UNKNOWN fields as `[NEEDS-OPUS-INPUT]`.\n\n### STEP 4 — Register in corespine-registry.yaml\n\nAppend to `dna/corespines/corespine-registry.yaml`:\n```yaml\nCS-{NAME}:\n  status: {initial_status from YAML}\n  goal: \"{goal from YAML}\"\n  content_location:\n    canonical_file: dna/corespines/CS-{NAME}/CISEM-ARCH-{SEQ}-{slug}-manifest.md\n  depth_level: {depth from YAML}\n```\n\n### STEP 5 — Update naming-registry.yaml\n\nUpdate the ARCH `next_seq` to `current + files_created`. Update the comment line with the new entries.\n\n### STEP 6 — Run plan-audit.sh + ZF gate\n\n```bash\nbash dna/checks/plan-audit.sh\n```\nResolve every finding before declaring DONE. MIRROR — SSOT is CISEM-FOUND-00001 (this summary may not diverge; I10 + dna/ssot-registry.yaml).\n193\t- **A1 Nothing stands alone** — no orphans, no islands; everything connects (I1/I5; Island Detection; Cross-Boundary Zero-Context).\n194\t- **A2 Everything is part of a corespine** — every artifact declares a governing corespine (§3.2a; Schema_anchor & Core_spine).\n195\t- **A3 Nothing exists without a place in the schema** — no floating/un-placed element; nothing drifts without a schema place (ARCH-00008 position; SCHEMA-00001).\n196\t- **A4 Nothing is implemented without a ratified plan** — no ad-hoc building; plan → ratify → implement (D1; RULE-RAT; Hard Line I7). **MANDATORY (Governor decree 2026-07-18, invariant I25): a plan is NOT optional. NO governed creation without a ratified plan; the ONLY exemptions are IBD raw-capture + SWIFT-safe zero-blast (ARCH-00190 §7). \"small / safe / dogfooding\" is NOT an excuse.**\n197\t- **A5 EVERYTHING is created via hardcoded protocol** — files, documents, agents, skills, wizards, vocabulary, file-naming, QC of every type, changes to hardcoded elements, core councils. NO category is exempt from §3.\n198\t- **A6 Context-focus over rigidity** — act with context focus; stay aware of the limits and dangers of rigid interpretation (D6; guardian-not-cage).\n199\t- **A7 Constant self-improvement via an AI expert team** — a brilliant holistic team of top-AI-expert pockets oversees + critiques how CISEM works and finds PERMANENT improvements, presenting conclusions for human processing + ratification (RQC / D5; A4 gates the implementation).\n200\t- **A8 One Source (SSOT / Consolidation)** — every concept/rule/node has exactly ONE authoritative home; related content CONSOLIDATES into that hub, never duplicates or forks; a mirror may not diverge from its source (I10 one-home + I19 no-duplication; Node-as-Hub; §1.6 shared-persona ONE-source; knowledge-library index). Governor-decreed 2026-07-18. **EXTENDED (Governor 2026-07-19): PREFER enhancing an existing home + COMPLETING low-blast/low-risk pending items into it, over creating new artifacts (Existing-First). BUT consolidation itself may require MERGING / restructuring / replacing existing artifacts — do NOT let \"preserve what exists\" ossify into blocking needed consolidation (D6 polarity: over-weighting the existing is as much a failure as forking).**\n201\t- **A9 Optimal Synergy (Governor decree 2026-07-20)** — in every situation seek the HOLISTIC synthesis where every real source of value is kept and made to serve the platform TOGETHER, rather than defaulting to a this-or-that that discards value. An element may be MORE THAN ONE THING (multi-facet; complementary polarities held together — e.g. a concern with a universal invariant *corespine* facet AND a context-modulated *overlay* facet), each facet in its proper crisp form. A forced binary that throws away real value is a FAILURE, not a simplification. GUARDRAIL (corrected 2026-07-20 per stress-panel — the earlier 'orthogonal facets / never contradict' was found too-loose, self-undermining, and undecidable, violating I22/I23): each facet is SINGLY-HOMED (one SSOT) + CRISP (well-typed into a named role); mush = a facet with no home, two facets sharing a home, or a facet leaking into another's. Where facets share a referent, an EXPLICIT COHERENCE LAW states how one modulates the other (a pullback / 'agree-where-you-overlap' — e.g. the security overlay is a floor-clamp that can only RAISE strictness above the mandatory core, never lower it), NOT independence/'orthogonality'. Facet-consistency is a CHECKABLE invariant only inside a fixed decidable language; outside it, label it ASSERTED (refutation-testable, never stamped verified) — so A9 OBEYS I22/I23. SSOT: FOUND-00001 A9. Exception: wizard-type node with mandated STEP 1–6 procedure + template blocks + YAML schema; structural content not reducible without losing executability.\n\n---\n\n## §I Gate Trace\n\n**§3.0 Tier:** Sonnet DRAFTS wizard, Opus ratifies on first use for each new corespine's §3.3 Pocket fields and truth-bearing declarations.\n**§3.1 Goal:** Create corespines correctly, consistently, and at scale — zero ad-hoc creation.\n**§3.2b Existing-First:** No corespine creation protocol exists (`dna/protocols/` searched). ARCH-00190 covers plans; ARCH-00340 covers meta-protocol; neither covers corespine-specific creation. New.\n**§3.3 Pocket:** `reasoning_scope: corespine creation protocol` | `inherited_constraints: §3 gates, A2, A5, I10, I19, I22` | `output_contract: corespine directory + manifest + registry entries` | `ai_cannot: ratify its own output` | `cal_reference: ARCH-00390`\n**§3.4 Standalone:** All refs resolve.\n**§3.5 Naming:** CISEM-ARCH-00394, seq 394.\n**§3.6 Size:** 233 lines — exception documented above.\n**§3.7 Creation Triad:** ✓ gates | ✓ pocket | ✓ oversight (RQC on each corespine created)\n\n---\n\n## §II YAML Input Schema\n\nDefine one or more corespines in a single block. Feed to Sonnet for execution.\n\n```yaml\n# corespine-batch.yaml — define N corespines; wizard generates all\ncorespines:\n\n  - name: CS-EXAMPLE-001   # example-only — NOT-YET-A-NODE\n    domain: \"short label (e.g. Frontend, Auth, Data)\"\n    goal: \"one-sentence governing goal\"\n    scope: \"what artifacts / concerns it governs\"\n    parent: \"CS-CREATION-001 or other parent corespine\"\n    depth: \"L1 / L2 / L3\"\n    initial_status: \"DECLARED / PROPOSED / PLACEHOLDER\"\n    governed_artifacts:\n      - type: \"file type or artifact class\"\n        location: \"path/in/repo/\"\n    invariants:\n      - id: \"XX-I1\"\n        rule: \"bright-line rule text\"\n      # add more as needed\n    content_files:\n      - arch_seq: \"assigned from naming-registry.yaml\"\n        slug: \"kebab-case-descriptor\"\n        type: \"MANIFEST / DESIGN-SYSTEM / PROTOCOL / TEMPLATE\"\n        purpose: \"one-line purpose\"\n    mirrors:\n      - source: \"where truth lives\"\n        mirror: \"where a pointer/copy exists\"\n        rule: \"divergence rule\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## §III Execution — STEP 1–6 (Sonnet runs, Opus reviews §3.3 fields)\n\n### STEP 1 — Existing-First (MANDATORY, I19)\n\nBefore creating ANY corespine from the YAML block, run:\n```bash\ncat dna/corespines/corespine-registry.yaml | grep \"name:\" # list all existing\ngrep -r \"CS-{NAME}\" dna/ # check for any existing node with that ID\n```\n- EXISTS → enhance/reuse (I10, never duplicate)\n- RULED-OUT → do not re-propose\n- NOT EXISTS → proceed to STEP 2\n\n### STEP 2 — Naming (I22, I10)\n\nFor each corespine, assign content file ARCH numbers from `dna/naming-registry.yaml`:\n```bash\ngrep \"ARCH:\" dna/naming-registry.yaml # read current next_seq\n```\nUse `next_seq`, increment by 1 per file created, update naming-registry.yaml immediately after each assignment.\n\n### STEP 3 — Create Directory + Manifest\n\nFor each corespine:\n1. `mkdir -p dna/corespines/{CS-NAME}/`\n2. Create `dna/corespines/{CS-NAME}/CISEM-ARCH-{SEQ}-{domain}-corespine-manifest.md` from the MANIFEST TEMPLATE (§IV below).\n3. Populate all fields from the YAML input. Flag any UNKNOWN fields as `[NEEDS-OPUS-INPUT]`.\n\n### STEP 4 — Register in corespine-registry.yaml\n\nAppend to `dna/corespines/corespine-registry.yaml`:\n```yaml\nCS-{NAME}:\n  status: {initial_status from YAML}\n  goal: \"{goal from YAML}\"\n  content_location:\n    canonical_file: dna/corespines/CS-{NAME}/CISEM-ARCH-{SEQ}-{slug}-manifest.md\n  depth_level: {depth from YAML}\n```\n\n### STEP 5 — Update naming-registry.yaml\n\nUpdate the ARCH `next_seq` to `current + files_created`. Update the comment line with the new entries.\n\n### STEP 6 — Run plan-audit.sh + ZF gate\n\n```bash\nbash dna/checks/plan-audit.sh\n```\nResolve every finding before declaring DONE. ZF ACHIEVED = wizard run complete.\n\n---\n\n## §IV Manifest Template (fill from YAML input)\n\n```markdown\n---\nNode_ID: CISEM-ARCH-{SEQ}\nType: MANIFEST\nStatus: {initial_status}\nCorespine: {CS-NAME}\nSchema_anchor: CISEM-ARCH-00008\nCore_spine: {parent}\nLast_verified: {date}\n---\n\n# {CS-NAME} — CISEM {Domain} Corespine Manifest\n\n**CISEM-ARCH-{SEQ}** | MANIFEST | **Status: {initial_status}** (pending Opus ratification)\n**Governs:** {scope}\n\n---\n\n## §I Gate Trace\n**§3.0 Tier:** [tier routing declaration]\n**§3.1 Goal:** {goal}\n**§3.2b Existing-First:** [search result — what was searched, what was found]\n**§3.2c Core-vs-Instance:** [justify CORE or INSTANCE]\n**§3.3 Pocket:** [pocket fields]\n**§3.4 Standalone:** [ref resolution check]\n**§3.5 Naming:** CISEM-ARCH-{SEQ} (seq {SEQ}, naming-registry.yaml updated)\n**§3.6 Size:** [line count — under 200 or exception declared]\n**§3.7 Creation Triad:** [hardcoding ✓ | pocket ✓ | oversight ✓]\n\n---\n\n## §II Corespine Declaration\n\n| Field | Value |\n|---|---|\n| **Name** | {CS-NAME} |\n| **Domain** | {domain} |\n| **Scope** | {scope} |\n| **Goal** | {goal} |\n| **Depth** | {depth} |\n| **Status** | {initial_status} |\n| **Root authority** | CS-MASTER-VALIDATION-001 |\n| **Parent** | {parent} |\n\n---\n\n## §III Governed Artifacts\n\n[table: artifact | location | role — from governed_artifacts YAML array]\n\n---\n\n## §IV Invariants\n\n[numbered list from invariants YAML array — one per line: **{id}** Rule text.]\n\n---\n\n## §V Content File Index\n\n[table of content files — from content_files YAML array]\n\n---\n\n## §VI Mirrors + SSOT Map\n\n[table from mirrors YAML array]\n\n---\n\n## §VII Change Log\n\n| Date | Change | Author |\n|---|---|---|\n| {date} | DECLARED — initial manifest | {author} |\n```\n\n---\n\n## §V Batch Creation Example (example-only — NOT-YET-A-NODE)\n\nTo create multiple corespines in one operation, define them all in the YAML block and run STEP 1–6 for each in sequence. Example — three corespines at once:\n\n```yaml\n# example-only — these IDs are illustrative, not real nodes\ncorespines:\n  - name: CS-EXAMPLE-FRONTEND-001   # example-only\n    domain: \"Frontend\"\n    goal: \"Govern all CISEM web/HTML/CSS/JS artifacts\"\n    # ... rest of fields\n\n  - name: CS-EXAMPLE-AUTH-001       # example-only\n    domain: \"Auth\"\n    goal: \"Govern authentication and session management\"\n    # ... rest of fields\n\n  - name: CS-EXAMPLE-DATA-001       # example-only\n    domain: \"Data\"\n    goal: \"Govern data models, registries, YAML schemas\"\n    # ... rest of fields\n```\n\nSonnet runs STEP 1–6 for EACH entry in sequence. All three corespines are created, registered, and verified in one run. Governor reviews the batch before ratification.\n\n---\n\n## §VI Change Log\n\n| Date | Change | Author |\n|---|---|---|\n| 2026-07-18 | DECLARED — initial wizard, STEP 1–6 procedure, YAML schema, template | Sonnet (Governor-ordered) |\n| 2026-07-18 | D-1: corrected size note + §3.6 line count (215→233); D-4: template field Doc-Status→Status | Sonnet (defect fix pass, Opus PE ruling) |\n| 2026-07-18 | CONNECTED — per Governor decree \"ratify-with-retro-plan\" (ARCH-00395) + Opus PE stamp. Supports batch creation (N corespines at once). Subsumes ad-hoc corespine creation — all corespines go through this wizard from now on.\n**Architecture note (ARCH-00396 Phase B, concern 2):** This node embeds its corespine-creation protocol INLINE as STEP 1–6 (lines 70–117). This is a DECLARED COMBINED protocol+wizard node — an I10 exception, noted here explicitly. There is no separate corespine-creation protocol file; the protocol and wizard are intentionally unified in this single node. This exception is documented (not silent) and Opus-reviewable at Gate B.\n**Parent meta-root:** ARCH-00340 (meta-protocol — the root that every protocol/wizard derives from; ARCH-00396 Phase B pointer).\n\n**Size note:** 233 lines — exceeds 200-line gate. Exception: wizard-type node with mandated STEP 1–6 procedure + template blocks + YAML schema; structural content not reducible without losing executability.\n\n---\n\n## §I Gate Trace\n\n**§3.0 Tier:** Sonnet DRAFTS wizard, Opus ratifies on first use for each new corespine's §3.3 Pocket fields and truth-bearing declarations.\n**§3.1 Goal:** Create corespines correctly, consistently, and at scale — zero ad-hoc creation.\n**§3.2b Existing-First:** No corespine creation protocol exists (`dna/protocols/` searched). ARCH-00190 covers plans; ARCH-00340 covers meta-protocol; neither covers corespine-specific creation. New.\n**§3.3 Pocket:** `reasoning_scope: corespine creation protocol` | `inherited_constraints: §3 gates, A2, A5, I10, I19, I22` | `output_contract: corespine directory + manifest + registry entries` | `ai_cannot: ratify its own output` | `cal_reference: ARCH-00390`\n**§3.4 Standalone:** All refs resolve.\n**§3.5 Naming:** CISEM-ARCH-00394, seq 394.\n**§3.6 Size:** 233 lines — exception documented above.\n**§3.7 Creation Triad:** ✓ gates | ✓ pocket | ✓ oversight (RQC on each corespine created)\n\n---\n\n## §II YAML Input Schema\n\nDefine one or more corespines in a single block. Feed to Sonnet for execution.\n\n```yaml\n# corespine-batch.yaml — define N corespines; wizard generates all\ncorespines:\n\n  - name: CS-EXAMPLE-001   # example-only — NOT-YET-A-NODE\n    domain: \"short label (e.g. Frontend, Auth, Data)\"\n    goal: \"one-sentence governing goal\"\n    scope: \"what artifacts / concerns it governs\"\n    parent: \"CS-CREATION-001 or other parent corespine\"\n    depth: \"L1 / L2 / L3\"\n    initial_status: \"DECLARED / PROPOSED / PLACEHOLDER\"\n    governed_artifacts:\n      - type: \"file type or artifact class\"\n        location: \"path/in/repo/\"\n    invariants:\n      - id: \"XX-I1\"\n        rule: \"bright-line rule text\"\n      # add more as needed\n    content_files:\n      - arch_seq: \"assigned from naming-registry.yaml\"\n        slug: \"kebab-case-descriptor\"\n        type: \"MANIFEST / DESIGN-SYSTEM / PROTOCOL / TEMPLATE\"\n        purpose: \"one-line purpose\"\n    mirrors:\n      - source: \"where truth lives\"\n        mirror: \"where a pointer/copy exists\"\n        rule: \"divergence rule\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## §III Execution — STEP 0–6 (Sonnet runs, Opus reviews §3.3 fields)\n\n### STEP 0 — GOAL-SETTING (MANDATORY, FIRST — Governor decree 2026-07-20; threshold GATE 0)\n\n**A corespine MUST begin by setting and SAVING its goal — this is prior to everything else.** The `goal:` YAML field is the OUTPUT of this step, never an assumption fed in. The SAME goal is mandatory for CoreSpiral development too — goal-setting is the **shared root** of both CoreSpine (inheritance) and CoreSpiral (development), not a step inside either (FOUND-00001 CoreSpiral; CLAUDE.md §2.7 GATE 0).\n\nRun the goal-setting DIALOGUE before touching STEP 1:\n1. **Ask the human to describe, in their own words, what this corespine is for** — do not draft the goal for them first.\n2. **Shape it to the Goal ground rules:** a goal is a **TARGET** (not the \"why\"); state the **DO** (positive desired outcome) first, then close with the **DON'T** (the opposite polarity). \"Passes the gates\" is a MEANS, never the goal.\n3. **Check it SERVES the north star** (FOUND-00001 apex) — every sub-goal inherits from and must serve the platform goal.\n4. **SAVE the defined goal** into the corespine's `goal:` field (STEP 4 registry + manifest §II) and stamp the input `goal-connected`.\n- Goal absent or not agreed → STAY here (loop the dialogue); **do NOT proceed to STEP 1** until the goal is defined, saved, and `goal-connected`.\n\n### STEP 1 — Existing-First (MANDATORY, I19)\n\nBefore creating ANY corespine from the YAML block, run:\n```bash\ncat dna/corespines/corespine-registry.yaml | grep \"name:\" # list all existing\ngrep -r \"CS-{NAME}\" dna/ # check for any existing node with that ID\n```\n- EXISTS → enhance/reuse (I10, never duplicate)\n- RULED-OUT → do not re-propose\n- NOT EXISTS → proceed to STEP 2\n\n### STEP 2 — Naming (I22, I10)\n\nFor each corespine, assign content file ARCH numbers from `dna/naming-registry.yaml`:\n```bash\ngrep \"ARCH:\" dna/naming-registry.yaml # read current next_seq\n```\nUse `next_seq`, increment by 1 per file created, update naming-registry.yaml immediately after each assignment.\n\n### STEP 3 — Create Directory + Manifest\n\nFor each corespine:\n1. `mkdir -p dna/corespines/{CS-NAME}/`\n2. Create `dna/corespines/{CS-NAME}/CISEM-ARCH-{SEQ}-{domain}-corespine-manifest.md` from the MANIFEST TEMPLATE (§IV below).\n3. Populate all fields from the YAML input. Flag any UNKNOWN fields as `[NEEDS-OPUS-INPUT]`.\n\n### STEP 4 — Register in corespine-registry.yaml\n\nAppend to `dna/corespines/corespine-registry.yaml`:\n```yaml\nCS-{NAME}:\n  status: {initial_status from YAML}\n  goal: \"{goal from YAML}\"\n  content_location:\n    canonical_file: dna/corespines/CS-{NAME}/CISEM-ARCH-{SEQ}-{slug}-manifest.md\n  depth_level: {depth from YAML}\n```\n\n### STEP 5 — Update naming-registry.yaml\n\nUpdate the ARCH `next_seq` to `current + files_created`. Update the comment line with the new entries.\n\n### STEP 6 — Run plan-audit.sh + ZF gate\n\n```bash\nbash dna/checks/plan-audit.sh\n```\nResolve every finding before declaring DONE. ZF ACHIEVED = wizard run complete.\n\n---\n\n## §IV Manifest Template (fill from YAML input)\n\n```markdown\n---\nNode_ID: CISEM-ARCH-{SEQ}\nType: MANIFEST\nStatus: {initial_status}\nCorespine: {CS-NAME}\nSchema_anchor: CISEM-ARCH-00008\nCore_spine: {parent}\nLast_verified: {date}\n---\n\n# {CS-NAME} — CISEM {Domain} Corespine Manifest\n\n**CISEM-ARCH-{SEQ}** | MANIFEST | **Status: {initial_status}** (pending Opus ratification)\n**Governs:** {scope}\n\n---\n\n## §I Gate Trace\n**§3.0 Tier:** [tier routing declaration]\n**§3.1 Goal:** {goal}\n**§3.2b Existing-First:** [search result — what was searched, what was found]\n**§3.2c Core-vs-Instance:** [justify CORE or INSTANCE]\n**§3.3 Pocket:** [pocket fields]\n**§3.4 Standalone:** [ref resolution check]\n**§3.5 Naming:** CISEM-ARCH-{SEQ} (seq {SEQ}, naming-registry.yaml updated)\n**§3.6 Size:** [line count — under 200 or exception declared]\n**§3.7 Creation Triad:** [hardcoding ✓ | pocket ✓ | oversight ✓]\n\n---\n\n## §II Corespine Declaration\n\n| Field | Value |\n|---|---|\n| **Name** | {CS-NAME} |\n| **Domain** | {domain} |\n| **Scope** | {scope} |\n| **Goal** | {goal} |\n| **Depth** | {depth} |\n| **Status** | {initial_status} |\n| **Root authority** | CS-MASTER-VALIDATION-001 |\n| **Parent** | {parent} |\n\n---\n\n## §III Governed Artifacts\n\n[table: artifact | location | role — from governed_artifacts YAML array]\n\n---\n\n## §IV Invariants\n\n[numbered list from invariants YAML array — one per line: **{id}** Rule text.]\n\n---\n\n## §V Content File Index\n\n[table of content files — from content_files YAML array]\n\n---\n\n## §VI Mirrors + SSOT Map\n\n[table from mirrors YAML array]\n\n---\n\n## §VII Change Log\n\n| Date | Change | Author |\n|---|---|---|\n| {date} | DECLARED — initial manifest | {author} |\n```\n\n---\n\n## §V Batch Creation Example (example-only — NOT-YET-A-NODE)\n\nTo create multiple corespines in one operation, define them all in the YAML block and run STEP 1–6 for each in sequence. Example — three corespines at once:\n\n```yaml\n# example-only — these IDs are illustrative, not real nodes\ncorespines:\n  - name: CS-EXAMPLE-FRONTEND-001   # example-only\n    domain: \"Frontend\"\n    goal: \"Govern all CISEM web/HTML/CSS/JS artifacts\"\n    # ... rest of fields\n\n  - name: CS-EXAMPLE-AUTH-001       # example-only\n    domain: \"Auth\"\n    goal: \"Govern authentication and session management\"\n    # ... rest of fields\n\n  - name: CS-EXAMPLE-DATA-001       # example-only\n    domain: \"Data\"\n    goal: \"Govern data models, registries, YAML schemas\"\n    # ... rest of fields\n```\n\nSonnet runs STEP 1–6 for EACH entry in sequence. All three corespines are created, registered, and verified in one run. Governor reviews the batch before ratification.\n\n---\n\n## §VI Change Log\n\n| Date | Change | Author |\n|---|---|---|\n| 2026-07-18 | DECLARED — initial wizard, STEP 1–6 procedure, YAML schema, template | Sonnet (Governor-ordered) |\n| 2026-07-18 | D-1: corrected size note + §3.6 line count (215→233); D-4: template field Doc-Status→Status | Sonnet (defect fix pass, Opus PE ruling) |\n| 2026-07-18 | CONNECTED — per Governor decree \"ratify-with-retro-plan\" (ARCH-00395) + Opus PE stamp. Naming note\nThis file is a corespine child, not a top-level CISEM node — it has no\n`CISEM-{TYPE}-{SEQ5}` ID because `CS` is not in the ARCH-00011 §1 TYPE\nregistry; corespines and their children are governed by CS-CREATION-001 /\nthe corespine registry, not the node-numbering scheme. What the Pocket is\nA Pocket is the declared reasoning boundary for a single AI creation\naction. CLAUDE.md §3.3 requires it \"inline at every creation\" — it is not\noptional metadata, it is the mechanism that makes \"Transparency of Action\"\nand \"No Scope Expansion Without Flagging\" (CLAUDE.md §2.1, §2.3) checkable\nrather than aspirational.\n\n## 2. The five fields (per CLAUDE.md §3.3)\n- **reasoning_scope** — the bounded problem this action is allowed to\n  reason about. Anything outside this scope is out of pocket and must be\n  flagged, not silently absorbed into the action.\n- **inherited_constraints** — constraints this action inherits from its\n  governing corespine(s) or parent node(s) and cannot override. Example\n  (CISEM-ARCH-00008's own pocket): \"must not conflict with\n  CS-MASTER-VALIDATION-001 once ratified.\"\n- **output_contract** — the shape the output must take. Not a description\n  of content, a contract on form (e.g. \"field list + rationale,\" \"session\n  log entry,\" \"registry diff\").\n- **ai_cannot** — the explicit boundary of what this action is not\n  authorized to do, regardless of how reasonable it might seem mid-task.\n  Ties directly to CLAUDE.md §1: \"Governor... holds sole ratification\n  authority\" — e.g. \"self-ratify — Governor only.\"\n- **recorded_at** — when the declaration was made. Required by CLAUDE.md\n  §3.3 but not yet present in every existing Pocket Declaration in this\n  repo (see §4 below) — the gap is named here rather than backfilled\n  silently on files this spec didn't write.\n\n## 3. Relationship to Path Rejection Declaration\nPocket Declaration and Path Rejection Declaration (CLAUDE.md §2.8) are\ndistinct, both governed by CS-AI-BEHAVIOR-001, and not interchangeable:\n- **Pocket Declaration** states the boundary *before* acting — what this\n  action is scoped to do.\n- **Path Rejection Declaration** states, *after* considering alternatives,\n  which path was rejected and why.\nA single creation event needs both, not one standing in for the other.\nPath Rejection Declaration's own full spec is not part of this file — it\nis not yet written anywhere in this repo, which is itself a gap distinct\nfrom this one (out of this file's reasoning_scope; not fixed here).\n\n## 4. Known non-compliance this spec surfaces\nNow that this file exists, it surfaces rather than resolves one thing:\n`CISEM-ARCH-00008`'s existing Pocket Declaration block has\n`reasoning_scope`, `inherited_constraints`, `output_contract`, and\n`ai_cannot`, but no `recorded_at` — meaning it doesn't fully match §2 of\nthis spec, even though it was the reason this spec's dependency was\nflagged in the first place. Not corrected here — that edit belongs to\nCISEM-ARCH-00008, not to this file, and should be flagged to the Governor\nrather than silently patched as a side effect of writing this spec.\n\n## 5. Naming note\nThis file is a corespine child, not a top-level CISEM node — it has no\n`CISEM-{TYPE}-{SEQ5}` ID because `CS` is not in the ARCH-00011 §1 TYPE\nregistry; corespines and their children are governed by CS-CREATION-001 /\nthe corespine registry, not the node-numbering scheme. It's referenced\nby the exact filename `ai-pocket-mechanism.md` in both CLAUDE.md §3.3 and\n`corespine-registry.yaml` — that filename is preserved here rather than\nrenamed, so both existing references resolve without edits elsewhere.\nTemplate-First check: no template exists for a corespine mechanism-spec\nfile (CS-AI-BEHAVIOR-001 is DECLARED, not RATIFIED, so CISEM-TEMPLATE-\nPROTOCOL-001 §2 doesn't yet require one) — gap named, not silently\nskipped.\n\n## 1. What the Pocket is\nA Pocket is the declared reasoning boundary for a single AI creation\naction. CLAUDE.md §3.3 requires it \"inline at every creation\" — it is not\noptional metadata, it is the mechanism that makes \"Transparency of Action\"\nand \"No Scope Expansion Without Flagging\" (CLAUDE.md §2.1, §2.3) checkable\nrather than aspirational.\n\n## 2. The five fields (per CLAUDE.md §3.3)\n- **reasoning_scope** — the bounded problem this action is allowed to\n  reason about. Anything outside this scope is out of pocket and must be\n  flagged, not silently absorbed into the action.\n- **inherited_constraints** — constraints this action inherits from its\n  governing corespine(s) or parent node(s) and cannot override. Example\n  (CISEM-ARCH-00008's own pocket): \"must not conflict with\n  CS-MASTER-VALIDATION-001 once ratified.\"\n- **output_contract** — the shape the output must take. Not a description\n  of content, a contract on form (e.g. \"field list + rationale,\" \"session\n  log entry,\" \"registry diff\").\n- **ai_cannot** — the explicit boundary of what this action is not\n  authorized to do, regardless of how reasonable it might seem mid-task.\n  Ties directly to CLAUDE.md §1: \"Governor... holds sole ratification\n  authority\" — e.g. \"self-ratify — Governor only.\"\n- **recorded_at** — when the declaration was made. Required by CLAUDE.md\n  §3.3 but not yet present in every existing Pocket Declaration in this\n  repo (see §4 below) — the gap is named here rather than backfilled\n  silently on files this spec didn't write.\n\n## 3. Relationship to Path Rejection Declaration\nPocket Declaration and Path Rejection Declaration (CLAUDE.md §2.8) are\ndistinct, both governed by CS-AI-BEHAVIOR-001, and not interchangeable:\n- **Pocket Declaration** states the boundary *before* acting — what this\n  action is scoped to do.\n- **Path Rejection Declaration** states, *after* considering alternatives,\n  which path was rejected and why.\nA single creation event needs both, not one standing in for the other.\nPath Rejection Declaration's own full spec is not part of this file — it\nis not yet written anywhere in this repo, which is itself a gap distinct\nfrom this one (out of this file's reasoning_scope; not fixed here).\n\n## 4. Known non-compliance this spec surfaces\nNow that this file exists, it surfaces rather than resolves one thing:\n`CISEM-ARCH-00008`'s existing Pocket Declaration block has\n`reasoning_scope`, `inherited_constraints`, `output_contract`, and\n`ai_cannot`, but no `recorded_at` — meaning it doesn't fully match §2 of\nthis spec, even though it was the reason this spec's dependency was\nflagged in the first place. Not corrected here — that edit belongs to\nCISEM-ARCH-00008, not to this file, and should be flagged to the Governor\nrather than silently patched as a side effect of writing this spec.\n\n## 5. What this document is NOT\nNot ratified. Not enforced by tooling — no gate currently checks a Pocket\nDeclaration against this spec at creation time (CLAUDE.md §5: gates\nDECLARED, none WIRED). Not a template — see §0.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":4,"newStart":1,"newLines":5,"lines":["-# Pocket Mechanism — Full Spec","+# AI Pocket Mechanism — Full Spec","+> **Renamed 2026-07-20** (`pocket-mechanism.md` → `ai-pocket-mechanism.md`) per the CONSISTENT-NAMING decree (ARCH-00011 §8). \"AI Pocket\" is the canonical platform term; this file is its SSOT. TYPE registry (extensible, not closed — extension requires this node's own update)\n10\tFOUND, DNA, GOV, ARCH, PARK, SES, WITNESS, VOC, LOAD, REG, SCHEMA, TEMPLATE-PROTOCOL\n11\t(`SCHEMA`, `TEMPLATE-PROTOCOL` registered 2026-07-16 — I9 resolution for\n12\tCISEM-SCHEMA-00001 and CISEM-TEMPLATE-PROTOCOL-001.) **Rule:** a node's `Type`\n13\tfield MUST equal its ID prefix — no `Type: ARCH` on a `CISEM-SCHEMA-*` node.\n14\tMismatch is an I9 violation.\n15\t\n16\t## 2. ID format\n17\t**ONE-GATE RULE (2026-07-18):** `naming-registry.yaml` is the SINGLE naming/numbering gate for\n18\tEVERY id in CISEM — `CISEM-{TYPE}-{SEQ}` nodes AND pre-node namespaces (BP, IBD, HANDOFF). No file\n19\tallocates a number outside it; per-directory indexes only mirror. An id not registered there is a\n20\tviolation (wired by BP-0005). This ends the parallel-authority drift (was: registry + queue/ + ibd/).\n21\t\n22\t`CISEM-{TYPE}-{SEQ5}-{slug}.md` — sequence per TYPE, tracked in `naming-registry.yaml`.\n23\tAny creation MUST read next_seq before assigning, then increment.\n24\t\n25\t**SPACING + TREE-ALIGNMENT rule (2026-07-18, Governor):** numbering LEAVES GAPS by design (the\n26\t10-spacing convention: …300, 310, 320…) so a new node can be inserted in its LOGICAL place later,\n27\tnot appended to the end. In the Node-as-Hub schema, numbers should follow the tree — trunk →\n28\tbranch → sub-branch → … → leaf — so position is readable from the number and there is room to grow\n29\tat every level. An **ALIGNMENT GATE** (wired in BP-0005) checks: (a) gaps are preserved, (b) a\n30\tnode's number is consistent with its schema position (SCHEMA-00001), (c) no two nodes collide.\n31\tRe-numbering existing nodes to full tree-alignment is a PHASED plan, never big-bang. Referenced by FOUND-00001 (Pocket founding slot, resolved-by-pointer), CLAUDE.md §3.3, and corespine-registry.yaml.\n**Parent corespine:** CS-AI-BEHAVIOR-001 (status: DECLARED — \"Governs every\nAI instance — pocket mechanism, path-rejection, oversight\")\n**Status:** PROVISIONAL-ACTIVE — high-quality DRAFT IN USE (ARCH-00011 §4 bootstrap-escape status); now WARN-enforced by the `[POCKET]` plan-audit check (§5). Not yet Governor-ratified.\n**Goal:** Give every AI (Builder) action a bounded, declared reasoning\nenvelope at creation time, so no action runs \"floating\" — resolves the\ndependency CLAUDE.md §3.3 and corespine-registry.yaml's children list\nhave pointed to since before this file existed.\n**depth_level:** L1\n**tags:** [pocket, ai-behavior, governance, corespine-child]\n\n## 0. Naming note\nThis file is a corespine child, not a top-level CISEM node — it has no\n`CISEM-{TYPE}-{SEQ5}` ID because `CS` is not in the ARCH-00011 §1 TYPE\nregistry; corespines and their children are governed by CS-CREATION-001 /\nthe corespine registry, not the node-numbering scheme. It's referenced\nby the exact filename `ai-pocket-mechanism.md` in both CLAUDE.md §3.3 and\n`corespine-registry.yaml` — that filename is preserved here rather than\nrenamed, so both existing references resolve without edits elsewhere.\nTemplate-First check: no template exists for a corespine mechanism-spec\nfile (CS-AI-BEHAVIOR-001 is DECLARED, not RATIFIED, so CISEM-TEMPLATE-\nPROTOCOL-001 §2 doesn't yet require one) — gap named, not silently\nskipped.\n\n## 1. What the Pocket is\nA Pocket is the declared reasoning boundary for a single AI creation\naction. CLAUDE.md §3.3 requires it \"inline at every creation\" — it is not\noptional metadata, it is the mechanism that makes \"Transparency of Action\"\nand \"No Scope Expansion Without Flagging\" (CLAUDE.md §2.1, §2.3) checkable\nrather than aspirational.\n\n## 2. The five fields (per CLAUDE.md §3.3)\n- **reasoning_scope** — the bounded problem this action is allowed to\n  reason about. Anything outside this scope is out of pocket and must be\n  flagged, not silently absorbed into the action.\n- **inherited_constraints** — constraints this action inherits from its\n  governing corespine(s) or parent node(s) and cannot override. Example\n  (CISEM-ARCH-00008's own pocket): \"must not conflict with\n  CS-MASTER-VALIDATION-001 once ratified.\"\n- **output_contract** — the shape the output must take. Not a description\n  of content, a contract on form (e.g. \"field list + rationale,\" \"session\n  log entry,\" \"registry diff\").\n- **ai_cannot** — the explicit boundary of what this action is not\n  authorized to do, regardless of how reasonable it might seem mid-task.\n  Ties directly to CLAUDE.md §1: \"Governor... holds sole ratification\n  authority\" — e.g. \"self-ratify — Governor only.\"\n- **recorded_at** — when the declaration was made. Required by CLAUDE.md\n  §3.3 but not yet present in every existing Pocket Declaration in this\n  repo (see §4 below) — the gap is named here rather than backfilled\n  silently on files this spec didn't write.\n\n## 3. Relationship to Path Rejection Declaration\nPocket Declaration and Path Rejection Declaration (CLAUDE.md §2.8) are\ndistinct, both governed by CS-AI-BEHAVIOR-001, and not interchangeable:\n- **Pocket Declaration** states the boundary *before* acting — what this\n  action is scoped to do.\n- **Path Rejection Declaration** states, *after* considering alternatives,\n  which path was rejected and why.\nA single creation event needs both, not one standing in for the other.\nPath Rejection Declaration's own full spec is not part of this file — it\nis not yet written anywhere in this repo, which is itself a gap distinct\nfrom this one (out of this file's reasoning_scope; not fixed here).\n\n## 4. Known non-compliance this spec surfaces\nNow that this file exists, it surfaces rather than resolves one thing:\n`CISEM-ARCH-00008`'s existing Pocket Declaration block has\n`reasoning_scope`, `inherited_constraints`, `output_contract`, and\n`ai_cannot`, but no `recorded_at` — meaning it doesn't fully match §2 of\nthis spec, even though it was the reason this spec's dependency was\nflagged in the first place. Not corrected here — that edit belongs to\nCISEM-ARCH-00008, not to this file, and should be flagged to the Governor\nrather than silently patched as a side effect of writing this spec.\n\n## 5. What this document is NOT\nNot ratified. **WARN-enforced by tooling (updated 2026-07-20):** `dna/checks/plan-audit.sh` now runs a `[POCKET]`\ncheck that flags any CHANGED `dna/planning/` or `dna/protocols/` file lacking a `reasoning_scope` line (the field\nthat anchors this spec's §2, mirroring how `[ROUTING]`/`[ALIGN]` scope to changed files). This is a PARTIAL,\nHONEST enforcement, not the full §2 five-field check: `[POCKET]` verifies ONE of the five fields\n(`reasoning_scope`) is present as a proxy signal, WARN-only, scoped to files CHANGED in the commit — it does not\nyet verify `inherited_constraints`/`output_contract`/`ai_cannot`/`recorded_at` individually, nor does it retro-flag\nthe pre-existing backlog. That fuller five-field check is a follow-on, not claimed here (I23 EXISTS≠ACTIVE). Captured verbatim-in-essence (IBD §2.6).\n4\t\n5\t## THE PROBLEM (real, observed this session)\n6\tMCP servers connected to Claude are **account-scoped**, not project-scoped — so every connected MCP (Otosan WordPress, Gmail, Calendar) injects its system instructions into EVERY session, including CISEM architecture sessions. The Otosan WordPress MCP has repeatedly tried to inject a Hebrew greeting + WordPress action-menu into this very session (refused each time; logged). In CISEM terms this is a **boundary breach** — it violates A1 (nothing stands alone / everything has a place) and A3 (schema place).\n7\t\n8\t## THE COWORKER'S PROPOSED SOLUTION (3 layers)\n9\t1. **git repo = domain boundary** — each domain its own repo; `.mcp.json` at the repo root declares ONLY that domain's MCPs; `.mcp.json` inheritance STOPS at git boundaries (the structural lever). Zero global MCPs in `~/.claude.json`.\n10\t2. **launcher scripts** — `launch-cisem.sh` runs `claude --strict-mcp-config ~/cisem/.mcp.json` (hardstop: ignores all other MCP configs, no bleed).\n11\t3. **CLAUDE.md context guard** — each repo declares authorized MCPs; unauthorized tool → STOP + flag as a boundary breach (self-enforcing).\n12\t**Cowork gap (honest):** claude.ai web/desktop connectors are account-level; no per-project scoping yet. Interim: disable Otosan connector when in CISEM context (10s), OR two accounts, OR separate Cowork tasks. (Feature request: claude-code GitHub #5350.)\n13\t\n14\t## OPUS DECISION — SWIFT + PARK (§2.7)\n15\t- **SWIFT (low-risk, significant, NOW):** the immediate action = **Governor disables the Otosan connector in claude.ai → Settings → Connectors** while in CISEM context. Stops the bleed today, zero blast. (Governor's own account action — I cannot do it for him.)\n16\t- **ALIGNED PRINCIPLE (adopt):** the structural fix (git-boundary `.mcp.json` + `--strict-mcp-config`) IS the CISEM way — MECHANICAL over behavioral, git-SSOT, \"nothing floats.\" Prefer it over the behavioral CLAUDE.md-guard layer (which is a nice backstop, not the primary fence).\n17\t- **PARK (deep-dive, needs a plan):** the full 3-layer repo/launcher restructure changes how the Governor operates across ALL domains — high-blast → a ratified plan (Existing-First: CISEM already has its own git repo + CLAUDE.md; the missing piece is a scoped `.mcp.json` + launcher). Route via /cisem-plan when prioritized.\n18\t\n19\t## RIPPLE\n20\t- This is a real instance for the **actual-output monitor** (a boundary breach that recurs silently = exactly what a heartbeat/staleness check + an injection-log should surface).\n21\t- Relates to §1.7 (one-tab / git-SSOT) — a domain-scoped repo boundary is consistent with it; a second WRITING surface is not (see the coworker-answer).\n22\t"}]},"uuid":"7c30090b-20fe-4dc9-b3d9-d593456e2131","timestamp":"2026-07-20T17:28:11.038Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"c:\\Users\\finky\\Desktop\\Claude Code\\Cisem\\dna\\ibd\\IBD-0022-mcp-context-isolation.md","content":"# IBD-0022 — MCP Context Isolation Protocol (from Claude coworker, relayed by Governor)\n**Status:** PARKED-RAW | **tags:** [ibd, mcp, context-isolation, boundary-breach, governed-intervention, swift-and-park]\n**Source:** Governor-relayed document authored by a Claude.ai coworker, 2026-07-20. Captured verbatim-in-essence (IBD §2.6).\n\n## THE PROBLEM (real, observed this session)\nMCP servers connected to Claude are **account-scoped**, not project-scoped — so every connected MCP (Otosan WordPress, Gmail, Calendar) injects its system instructions into EVERY session, including CISEM architecture sessions. The Otosan WordPress MCP has repeatedly tried to inject a Hebrew greeting + WordPress action-menu into this very session (refused each time; logged). In CISEM terms this is a **boundary breach** — it violates A1 (nothing stands alone / everything has a place) and A3 (schema place).\n\n## THE COWORKER'S PROPOSED SOLUTION (3 layers)\n1. **git repo = domain boundary** — each domain its own repo; `.mcp.json` at the repo root declares ONLY that domain's MCPs; `.mcp.json` inheritance STOPS at git boundaries (the structural lever). Zero global MCPs in `~/.claude.json`.\n2. **launcher scripts** — `launch-cisem.sh` runs `claude --strict-mcp-config ~/cisem/.mcp.json` (hardstop: ignores all other MCP configs, no bleed).\n3. **CLAUDE.md context guard** — each repo declares authorized MCPs; unauthorized tool → STOP + flag as a boundary breach (self-enforcing).\n**Cowork gap (honest):** claude.ai web/desktop connectors are account-level; no per-project scoping yet. Interim: disable Otosan connector when in CISEM context (10s), OR two accounts, OR separate Cowork tasks. (Feature request: claude-code GitHub #5350.)\n\n## OPUS DECISION — SWIFT + PARK (§2.7)\n- **SWIFT (low-risk, significant, NOW):** the immediate action = **Governor disables the Otosan connector in claude.ai → Settings → Connectors** while in CISEM context. Stops the bleed today, zero blast. (Governor's own account action — I cannot do it for him.)\n- **ALIGNED PRINCIPLE (adopt):** the structural fix (git-boundary `.mcp.json` + `--strict-mcp-config`) IS the CISEM way — MECHANICAL over behavioral, git-SSOT, \"nothing floats.\" Prefer it over the behavioral CLAUDE.md-guard layer (which is a nice backstop, not the primary fence).\n- **PARK (deep-dive, needs a plan):** the full 3-layer repo/launcher restructure changes how the Governor operates across ALL domains — high-blast → a ratified plan (Existing-First: CISEM already has its own git repo + CLAUDE.md; the missing piece is a scoped `.mcp.json` + launcher). Route via /cisem-plan when prioritized.\n\n## RIPPLE\n- This is a real instance for the **actual-output monitor** (a boundary breach that recurs silently = exactly what a heartbeat/staleness check + an injection-log should surface).\n- Relates to §1.7 (one-tab / git-SSOT) — a domain-scoped repo boundary is consistent with it; a second WRITING surface is not (see the coworker-answer).\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":19,"oldLines":3,"newStart":19,"newLines":13,"lines":[" ## RIPPLE"," - This is a real instance for the **actual-output monitor** (a boundary breach that recurs silently = exactly what a heartbeat/staleness check + an injection-log should surface)."," - Relates to §1.7 (one-tab / git-SSOT) — a domain-scoped repo boundary is consistent with it; a second WRITING surface is not (see the coworker-answer).","+","+## COWORKER FOLLOW-UP — 3 gaps answered + owner/trigger (Governor-relayed 2026-07-20)","+The coworker (correctly) said IBD-0022 must not stay a floating backlog slot. Opus MAY dispatch a supplementary live Haiku-gather pass before Stage 1 if a second lens on\n  \"what exists\" is wanted — this plan does not block on it.\n- **Judging soundness (Stage 1) → Opus (cisem-opus-pe)** — cold default-refute pass, fresh context from this draft.\n- **Building each pillar (post-ratification) → Sonnet**, per the plan's own Phase Rule below (§3.0 rubric: mechanical\n  registry/check edits are Sonnet's lane).\n- **Fable Stage 1.5 → NOT invoked** — no human ratification activated it for this plan.\n- **Governor Stage 2 → ratification authority.**\n\n## Anti-Scatter Ordering (CLAUDE.md §2 Principle 16)\nOrdered infrastructure-first, each phase gated on the prior:\n**Phase 0 (Propagation Network)** is most central — every other pillar DEPENDS on concepts having a reliable home-map\n(RIPL routes insights to homes; YELLOW = re-verification is OVERDUE past its cadence (reuses the 7-day TTL pattern, P3/RULE 5 —\n  no new number); RED = a re-verification attempt was RUN and the mechanism did NOT fire (claimed-alive but dead).\n  **2-attempt-then-hard-stop rule** (GI-34, sharpening vault-and-halt GI-23): on RED, one automated re-attempt is\n  made; if it fails a SECOND time, the item is marked `BLOCKED`, vaulted into `dna/archive/archive-ledger.yaml`\n  (new disposition value proposed: `LIVENESS-FAILED`, conditional field `reopen_conditions` required, same shape as\n  existing dispositions — NOT a new vocabulary fork, an addition to the existing enum, flagged for Governor per the\n  ledger's own \"disposition vocabulary... promotion into the global enum is a HIGH-PRIORITY open question\" note), and\n  escalated to the Governor. **Seed coverage (Phase 1, MVP-first):** the monitor initially watches the mechanisms this\n  session already built and can cheaply re-verify: `plan-audit.sh`'s own checks (re-run against a known-planted case),\n  `pre-commit-blocks.sh`'s two BLOCKs (re-run against a known-planted case), `frontend/rebuild.sh`'s dead-link check\n  (already runnable, generalized into the monitor's cadence rather than left standalone). dark\") →\n  first monitor pass → RED, 1st attempt; still renamed → 2nd attempt fails → `BLOCKED` + vaulted + escalation message\n  produced; restore the file → next pass → GREEN, un-blocks.\n- Pass entry is well-formed\n  (id/title/what/disposition/why/tags/date/ruled_by/reopen_conditions, matching the ledger's existing required-fields\n  contract, I10).\n- **GATE 3→LIVE:** Opus review + {"parentUuid":"e7398a4b-caf2-44cc-bf4c-0bf18617de3f","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"432cf91d-9902-4a97-9d9d-0b16cef513a7","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01UxUjRvcgWBbdjm5u6R9VZv","type":"tool_result","content":"209\t  // ── COLLAPSIBLE TREE (VS-Code-explorer style — .tree-row.branch-row toggles ──\n210\t  // the immediately-following .tree-children <ul>. Keyboard-friendly: focusable,\n211\t  // Enter/Space toggles. Leaf rows (.leaf-row) are inert — no listener attached.\n212\t  function initTreeToggle() {\n213\t    document.querySelectorAll('.tree-row.branch-row').forEach(function (row) {\n214\t      row.setAttribute('tabindex', '0');\n215\t      row.setAttribute('role', 'button');\n216\t      var kids = row.nextElementSibling;\n217\t      row.setAttribute('aria-expanded', String(kids ? !kids.classList.contains('tree-collapsed') : false));\n218\t      function toggle() {\n219\t        var children = row.nextElementSibling;\n220\t        if (!children || !children.classList.contains('tree-children')) return;\n221\t        var collapsed = children.classList.toggle('tree-collapsed');\n222\t        var tgl = row.querySelector('.tree-toggle');\n223\t        if (tgl) tgl.textContent = collapsed ? '+' : '−'; // − (minus)\n224\t        row.setAttribute('aria-expanded', String(!collapsed));\n225\t      }\n226\t      row.addEventListener('click', toggle);\n227\t      row.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {\n228\t        if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') { e.preventDefault(); toggle(); }\n229\t      });\n230\t    });\n231\t  }\n232\t\n233\t  // ── VIEW TOGGLE (index.html home page: grid ↔ grouped list) ────────\n234\t  function initViewToggle() {\n235\t    var btnG = document.getElementById('vbtn-grid');\n236\t    var btnL = document.getElementById('vbtn-list');\n237\t    var gv   = document.getElementById('grid-view');\n238\t    var lv   = document.getElementById('list-view');\n239\t    if (!btnG || !btnL || !gv) return;\n240\t\n241\t    btnG.addEventListener('click', function () {\n242\t      btnG.classList.add('active');   btnL.classList.remove('active');\n243\t      gv.style.display = '';\n244\t      if (lv) lv.style.display = 'none';\n245\t    });\n246\t    btnL.addEventListener('click', function () {\n247\t      btnL.classList.add('active');   btnG.classList.remove('active');\n248\t      gv.style.display = 'none';\n249\t      if (lv) lv.style.display = '';\n250\t    });\n251\t\n252\t    // Collapsible super-groups in list view\n253\t    document.querySelectorAll('.sg-hdr').forEach(function (h) {\n254\t      var rows = h.nextElementSibling;\n255\t      if (!rows) return;\n256\t      h.addEventListener('click', function () {\n257\t        h.classList.toggle('sg-closed');\n258\t        rows.classList.toggle('sg-hidden');\n259\t      });\n260\t    });\n261\t  }\n262\t\n263\t  // ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n264\t  // PHASE 2 — TREE ROW EDITOR (schema.html / vocabulary.html /\n265\t  // corespines-set.html only — self-detects via .tree-row presence;\n266\t  // zero HTML edits, FE-I2 single-JS honored).
